title: Kodomo (musician)
text:
Kodomo (musician)

Kodomo is the solo musical project of Chris Childs, an American composer, producer, and performer based in Boulder, Colorado, USA. Childs combines elements of glitch, IDM, and ambient music with organic instrumentation and field recordings to create sonic environments that are sometimes beautiful, sometimes eerie, and always meticulously crafted.

In live performances, Childs uses a unique setup that combines Ableton Live with various keyboards, controllers, and effect processors to create a organic and constantly evolving soundscape.

Since its inception in 2004, Kodomo has released three full-length albums, one mini-album, and several singles and remixes on a variety of independent labels. In 2009, Kodomo signed with German label Ghostly International and released his fourth album, Patterns & Light.

Childs has also composed music for film, television, and video games, including the award-winning score for the independent game Machinarium.

title: Elisha Bushnell House
text:
The Elisha Bushnell House is a historic house in the town of West Hartford, Connecticut. It is located on the corner of Farmington Avenue and Prospect Avenue, in a predominantly residential area. The house was built in 1768 by Elisha Bushnell, a prominent Hartford merchant, and has been owned by his descendants ever since. It was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1998.

The Elisha Bushnell House is a 2-1/2 story wood frame structure, with a gabled roof and clapboarded exterior. It is five bays wide, with the main entrance in the center bay, flanked by sidelight windows and topped by a fanlight. The interior follows a center hall plan, with a parlor to one side and a dining room to the other, each with a fireplace. A narrow staircase rises behind the hall, and there are two additional rooms on the second floor. A later 20th-century addition extends to the rear of the house.

The house was built in 1768 by Elisha Bushnell, a prominent Hartford merchant, and has been owned by his descendants ever since. It was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1998.

title: Mary Williams
text:
Mary Williams (1740-1814) was an English actress.

She was born in London. Her father was an actor and her mother was a dancer. Williams made her stage debut at the age of six. She appeared in many plays in London, including The Recruiting Officer (1754) and The Beaux' Stratagem (1758).

In 1759, she married the actor David Garrick. They had two children.

Williams retired from the stage in 1769. After Garrick's death in 1779, she lived in retirement until her own death in 1814.

title: Cold is the Grave
text: In ‘Cold is the Grave’, Peter Robinson’s sixth Inspector Banks novel, Banks is involved in a cold case that strikes close to home. When a little girl, Emily, goes missing from her school, Banks is asked to investigate, and as he starts digging, he finds a connection between the disappearance and a series of unsolved child murders. With time running out and the pressure mounting, Banks has to navigate his way through a web of lies and secrets in order to uncover the truth and bring the child home safely. In the process he has to face up to his own demons and is forced to examine the dark side of his supposedly idyllic home. Robinson’s trademark combination of suspense and psychological insight makes for a gripping and atmospheric thriller that will keep the reader on tenterhooks until the very last page.

title: Microsoft seeking spyware trojan
text:
"IBM has instructed software safety professionals to use a virus authoring kit to develop a Trojan Horse program for its testing.

The company asked experts to attend its annual Risk Research Conference next year to learn of the request.

Some researchers said offering Microsoft a bug in this way was unacceptable.

But the firm stated it needed to test its encryption software against the most complex attacks.

IBM has offered the assistance of safety professionals to let it identify flaws in its technology in the past to determine any flaws it develops can be quickly corrected.

Dangerous

A Trojan Horse - named after the method used by Greek heroes to enter Troy - is a kind of computer virus that masquerades as a legitimate program or file.

Once activated, a Trojan Horse can erase data or perform other malicious or intrusive behaviors.

IBM has been requesting scientists to take part in a day-long session on 24-25 March where they will be asked to use the Red Widow virus authoring kit to make a Trojan Horseresource that will be supplied to the company.

The firm said a trojan horse, virus or worm exploiting this source could be designed to attack products to be tested.

Intel stated no vulnerability found should be too complex in its design so as to make research impossible."

title: Rethinking BiSeNet For Real-time Semantic Segmentation
text:
BiSeNet has been proved to be a popular two-stream network for real-time
segmentation. However, its principle of adding an extra path to encode spatial
information is time-consuming, and the backbones borrowed from pretrained
tasks, e.g., image classification, may be inefficient for image segmentation
due to the deficiency of task-specific design. To handle these problems, we
propose a novel and efficient structure named Short-Term Dense Concatenate
network (STDC network) by removing structure redundancy. Specifically, we
gradually reduce the dimension of feature maps and use the aggregation of them
for image representation, which forms the basic module of STDC network. In the
decoder, we propose a Detail Aggregation module by integrating the learning of
spatial information into low-level layers in single-stream manner. Finally, the
low-level features and deep features are fused to predict the final
segmentation results. Extensive experiments on Cityscapes and CamVid dataset
demonstrate the effectiveness of our method by achieving promising trade-off
between segmentation accuracy and inference speed. On Cityscapes, we achieve
71.9% mIoU on the test set with a speed of 250.4 FPS on NVIDIA GTX 1080Ti,
which is 45.2% faster than the latest methods, and achieve 76.8% mIoU with 97.0
FPS while inferring on higher resolution images.

title: The Book of Dreams
text: The principal character of The Book of Dreams is Seraphina, who lives in the city of Medellia, and who has the rare faculty of entering into the dreams of other people. She finds that she has this power, when she translates the veiled dream of the prince, who is subject to frequent recurrences of nightmare. This occurrence predicts a disaster, which is calculated to overturn the destiny of Medellia. Seraphina, called to the court of the prince, enters the nocturnal scenes of the prince’s dream, in order to discover the cause of the disturbance and to find a solution to prevent the approaching catastrophe. In this parallel world, Seraphina is confronted with the most frightful and appalling scenes which she has herself painted. But in this parallel world she meets some strange allies, a lion with silver hair, a company of wanderers in the region of dreams, and a mysterious figure clad in stars. While she struggles to explain the meaning of the symbols, and save the city, she pursues a personal journey of self-discovery. It is only after a long process of grappling with her own past, and the recognition of her own inherited power, that she finally realizes that the salvation of Medellia lies in the understanding of her own enigmatic dreams. The Book of Dreams is an enthralling tale of the discovery of inner courage, the power of friendship, and the transformative nature of dreams, in times of crisis. The enigmatic structure of the novel, and the depiction of the nocturnal world, will stimulate the reader’s imagination and make him reflect on the mysterious power of dreams. Will Seraphina succeed in her mission, and save her city, and herself, or will she remain forever in the land of dreams?

title: Kernelized Weighted SUSAN based Fuzzy C-Means Clustering for Noisy Image Segmentation
text:
The paper proposes a novel Kernelized image segmentation scheme for noisy
images that utilizes the concept of Smallest Univalue Segment Assimilating
Nucleus (SUSAN) and incorporates spatial constraints by computing circular
colour map induced weights. Fuzzy damping coefficients are obtained for each
nucleus or center pixel on the basis of the corresponding weighted SUSAN area
values, the weights being equal to the inverse of the number of horizontal and
vertical moves required to reach a neighborhood pixel from the center pixel.
These weights are used to vary the contributions of the different nuclei in the
Kernel based framework. The paper also presents an edge quality metric obtained
by fuzzy decision based edge candidate selection and final computation of the
blurriness of the edges after their selection. The inability of existing
algorithms to preserve edge information and structural details in their
segmented maps necessitates the computation of the edge quality factor (EQF)
for all the competing algorithms. Qualitative and quantitative analysis have
been rendered with respect to state-of-the-art algorithms and for images ridden
with varying types of noises. Speckle noise ridden SAR images and Rician noise
ridden Magnetic Resonance Images have also been considered for evaluating the
effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in extracting important segmentation
information.

title:
Linking Cellular and Mechanical Processes in Articular Cartilage Lesion
  Formation: A Mathematical Model
text:
A severe application of stress on articular cartilage can initiate a cascade
of biochemical reactions that can lead to the development of osteoarthritis. We
constructed a multiscale mathematical model of the process with three
components: cellular, chemical, and mechanical. The cellular component
describes the different chondrocyte states according to the chemicals these
cells release. The chemical component models the change in concentrations of
those chemicals. The mechanical component contains a simulation of pressure
application onto a cartilage explant and the resulting strains that initiate
the biochemical processes. The model creates a framework for incorporating
explicit mechanics, simulated by finite element analysis, into a theoretical
biology framework.

title: Mixture Modeling of Global Shape Priors and Autoencoding Local Intensity Priors for Left Atrium Segmentation
text:
Left atrium segmentation is a crucial step in the diagnosis and treatment of various cardiac conditions. Accurate segmentation of the left atrium (LA) can help clinicians to identify potential risks and plan appropriate interventions. However, LA segmentation remains a challenging task due to the complexity of the heart's anatomy and the variability of the LA's shape and appearance across individuals.

In this paper, we propose a novel approach to LA segmentation that combines global shape priors and autoencoding local intensity priors using a mixture modeling framework. Our approach leverages the strengths of both global and local prior knowledge to improve the accuracy and robustness of LA segmentation.

We first establish a global shape prior using a statistical shape model, which captures the average shape and variability of the LA across a population. We then combine the global shape prior with a local intensity prior, which is learned from a set of training images using an autoencoder network. The autoencoder network is trained to reconstruct the input images, and the learned local intensity prior is used to capture the spatial patterns and variability of the LA's intensity values.

We propose a mixture modeling framework that combines the global shape prior and local intensity prior to segment the LA. The mixture modeling framework allows us to integrate the global and local priors in a probabilistic manner, enabling the model to adapt to the complexity and variability of the LA's shape and appearance.

We evaluate our approach on a dataset of cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) images and compare it with state-of-the-art methods. Our results show that our approach outperforms the compared methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness. We also perform a series of ablation studies to analyze the contributions of the global shape prior and local intensity prior, demonstrating the effectiveness of our mixture modeling approach.

Our proposed approach has the potential to improve the accuracy and efficiency of LA segmentation, which can ultimately contribute to better diagnosis and treatment of cardiac conditions.

title: Those of you who are mixed Syrian + Lebanese, how do you identify?

Being mixed has allowed me to experience and appreciate different perspectives and cultures in a way that might not have been possible otherwise. Sure, there can be challenges too, like feeling like an outsider in both cultures or dealing with stereotypes from each side. But overall, I feel grateful for the diversity and complexity of my background. It's something that makes me unique and allows me to connect with people on multiple levels. So, tell us your stories! title: Gregory Baum
text:
Gregory Baum (born January 23, 1923 in Hirschberg an der Ries, Germany) is a Canadian Roman Catholic theologian and sociologist. He is considered one of the most prominent figures of Canadian theology.

Baum was born to a Jewish family, but his parents converted to Christianity when he was a child. He studied at the Sorbonne in Paris and at the University of Toronto. He was ordained a priest in 1949, and he later obtained a doctorate in theology from the University of Münster.

Baum's main areas of interest are ecumenism, social ethics, and the sociology of religion. He has been a member of the Pontifical Council for Promoting Christian Unity and the International Theological Commission. He is currently a member of the Doctrine Commission of the Canadian Conference of Catholic Bishops.

title: CUSUM Filter for Brain Segmentation on DSC Perfusion MR Head Scans with Abnormal Brain Anatomy
text:
This paper proposes a novel approach to brain segmentation using a modified cumulative sum (CUSUM) filter on digital subtraction perfusion magnetic resonance (DSC-MR) head scans with abnormal brain anatomy. The CUSUM filter is widely used in signal processing and control systems, but has not been previously applied to medical image segmentation. In this study, we adapt the CUSUM filter to address the challenges of segmenting brains with abnormal anatomy, which can be difficult to accurately separate from the surrounding tissue using traditional methods.

Our proposed method uses the CUSUM filter to calculate a statistical boundary between the brain and non-brain tissues based on the pixel intensity values in the DCS-MR images. We apply the filter to a series of 2D slices from the 3D imaging data, and then use a clustering algorithm to group pixels into different tissue classes. We evaluate our method using a dataset of 10 DSC-MR head scans with abnormal brain anatomy, and compare the results to those obtained using traditional machine learning approaches.

The results show that the CUSUM filter outperforms traditional methods in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. Specifically, it achieves higher accuracy in segmenting brains with abnormal anatomy, while also being computationally faster than other methods. Additionally, the CUSUM filter provides more consistent performance across different subjects and scan sessions, indicating its potential for robust clinical application.

This work highlights the potential of the CUSUM filter as a useful tool for brain segmentation in DSC-MR head scans, particularly when dealing with abnormal brain anatomy. Future research directions include further optimizing the filter parameters and exploring its applicability to other types of medical images.

title: Similar submodules and coincidence site modules
text:
We consider connections between similar sublattices and coincidence site
lattices (CSLs), and more generally between similar submodules and coincidence
site modules of general (free) $\mathbb{Z}$-modules in $\mathbb{R}^d$.
  In particular, we generalise results obtained by S. Glied and M. Baake [1,2]
on similarity and coincidence isometries of lattices and certain lattice-like
modules called $\mathcal{S}$-modules. An important result is that the factor
group $\mathrm{OS}(M)/\mathrm{OC}(M)$ is Abelian for arbitrary
$\mathbb{Z}$-modules $M$, where $\mathrm{OS}(M)$ and $\mathrm{OC}(M)$ are the
groups of similar and coincidence isometries, respectively. In addition, we
derive various relations between the indices of CSLs and their corresponding
similar sublattices.
  [1] S. Glied, M. Baake, Similarity versus coincidence rotations of lattices,
Z. Krist. 223, 770--772 (2008). DOI: 10.1524/zkri.2008.1054
  [2] S. Glied, Similarity and coincidence isometries for modules, Can. Math.
Bull. 55, 98--107 (2011). DOI: 10.4153/CMB-2011-076-x

title: Foreground Clustering for Joint Segmentation and Localization in Videos and Images
text:
In this paper, we propose a novel approach to joint segmentation and localization in videos and images called Foreground Clustering. The proposed method leverages the strengths of both spectral clustering and graph-based algorithms to simultaneously segment objects from their backgrounds and estimate their positions within the scene.

Existing methods often treat these tasks separately, requiring manual parameter tuning and resulting in suboptimal performance when dealing with complex scenes or varying illumination conditions. In contrast, our method treats the problems as interrelated and uses them to mutually improve each other. By iteratively refining object boundaries and motion estimates through careful cluster assignments, Foreground Clustering achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on several benchmark datasets while providing real-time performance.

The key idea is to construct an affinity graph that encodes appearance, spatial, and temporal information across frames and then applies spectral clustering to partition it into coherent foreground structures. These are then used to seed dense trajectory optimization, which revises object boundaries based on motion cues and enforces temporal consistency. This process alternates between clustering and tracking until convergence, where the final output consists of separated objects and their associated motion fields.

Extensive experiments show that Foreground Clustering outperforms existing methods under various scenarios, such as occlusions, cluttered scenes, shadows, and low light conditions. Additionally, its ability to handle irregular object shapes and non-rigid deformations makes it particularly suitable for applications like multi-object tracking, activity recognition, and video surveillance. Overall, the proposed method significantly advances the field by introducing a robust solution that can effectively address challenging scenarios in computer vision.

title: I'm scarred for life and I don't think I'll ever cut again
text:
I've been struggling with self-harm for years, and I thought that cutting was my way of coping with my emotions. But yesterday, something happened that changed everything.

I was in a particularly bad place, feeling overwhelmed by my thoughts and feelings, and I started to cut myself. It wasn't anything new - I've done it countless times before - but this time, something felt different. As I looked at my arms, covered in blood and scars, I realized that this wasn't helping me. It wasn't making me feel better. In fact, it was only making things worse.

For the first time, I saw my scars for what they really were: a constant reminder of my pain and suffering. They weren't a sign of strength or resilience; they were a symbol of my failure to cope with my problems in a healthy way. And as I stared at them, I knew that I couldn't keep doing this to myself. I had to find another way.

It hasn't been easy, but I've been trying to find alternative ways to cope with my emotions. I've been talking to a therapist, practicing mindfulness, and finding other outlets for my stress and anxiety. It's still hard, and some days are definitely easier than others, but I know that I can't go back to cutting. Not after seeing how much damage it's done to my body and my mind.

I know that I'll always have these scars, physical and emotional, but I'm determined to make sure that they don't define me. I want to move forward, to heal and grow, and to learn how to love myself without hurting myself. It won't be easy, but I'm ready to try.

title: Cross-Modal Progressive Comprehension for Referring Segmentation
text:
In this paper, we present a novel approach to referring segmentation that leverages cross-modal progressive comprehension to improve object segmentation in images. Referring segmentation is the task of segregating objects in an image based on their mentions in natural language descriptions. Existing approaches have relied heavily on visual features and suffer from limitations in handling complex scenes with multiple objects or non-descriptive language. Our proposed method addresses these challenges by incorporating cognitive theories of human language understanding and vision, which posits that humans use language to guide attention and eye movements when describing visual stimuli.

We propose a two-stage framework that first generates region proposals using a DeepLabv3+ model and then refines them using a Cross-Modal Attention Module (CMAM). The CMAM integrates information from both modalities through multi-layer perceptron networks, allowing it to learn how to weigh the importance of different words in relation to the visual context. We evaluate our model on three benchmark datasets and show significant improvements over existing methods, especially in cases where the language description contains incomplete or ambiguous information.

Our experiments also provide insights into the role of each modality in referring segmentation, revealing that both visual and linguistic cues play crucial roles in achieving optimal performance. Furthermore, we analyze the effectiveness of our attention mechanism and demonstrate its ability to focus on relevant regions and dismiss irrelevant ones, even in presence of distractors. Overall, this work represents an important step towards developing more accurate and robust real-time referring segmentation systems that can enable improved scene understanding capabilities for various applications such as robotics, autonomous vehicles, and virtual assistants.

title: Weighted Sobolev Spaces on Metric Measure Spaces
text:
We investigate weighted Sobolev spaces on metric measure spaces $(X,d,m)$.
Denoting by $\rho$ the weight function, we compare the space $W^{1,p}(X,d,\rho
m)$ (which always concides with the closure $H^{1,p}(X,d,\rho m)$ of Lipschitz
functions) with the weighted Sobolev spaces $W^{1,p}_\rho(X,d,m)$ and
$H^{1,p}_\rho(X,d,m)$ defined as in the Euclidean theory of weighted Sobolev
spaces. Under mild assumptions on the metric measure structure and on the
weight we show that $W^{1,p}(X,d,\rho m)=H^{1,p}_\rho(X,d, m)$. We also adapt
results by Muckenhoupt and recent work by Zhikov to the metric measure setting,
considering appropriate conditions on $\rho$ that ensure the equality
$W^{1,p}_\rho(X,d,m)=H^{1,p}_\rho(X,d,m)$.

title: Fine-Grained Segmentation Networks: Self-Supervised Segmentation for Improved Long-Term Visual Localization
text:
In this paper, we propose a novel approach to long-term visual localization that leverages fine-grained segmentation networks (FGSN) for improved performance. Existing methods for visual localization rely on coarse segmentation techniques that often result in reduced accuracy and robustness. FGSN addresses this limitation by introducing a self-supervised segmenation framework that learns to segment images at multiple scales and levels of detail. This allows for more accurate and robust feature extraction, resulting in improved localization performance.

Our experimental results show that FGSN outperforms state-of-the-art methods on several challenging benchmark datasets, including those with varying illumination conditions, viewpoints, and occlusions. We also demonstrate the generalizability of our approach by evaluating it on real-world scenarios, where FGSN shows superior performance compared to traditional localization methods.

The key contribution of this work is the introduction of a novel architecture that integrates a self-supervised segmentation network with a convolutional neural network (CNN) for visual localization. The proposed architecture enables the learning of fine-grained features that are essential for reliable long-term localization. Our extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of FGSN and establish it as a new baseline for visual localization tasks.

title: Peter Gottfried Kremsner
text:
Christoph Karl Kremsner (born 16 June 1961 in Wien Neustadt, Vienna) is a consultant in tropical medicine and Full Professor at the University of Heidelberg, Germany. since 1992 he has been leading the Center de Recherches Médicales en Gabon (CERMEL), Cameroon, now as director. For about two centuries Kremsner has played an influential role in the international study of tropical infectious diseases. Biography
Kremsner grew up in Sigleß, Vienna. He studied pharmacy at the University of Salzburg and graduated as a Doctor of Science in 1985. He began his scientific career as a clinical professor at the Department of Specific Prophylaxis and Tropical Surgery, University of Bucharest. 1987 he moved to Portugal studying there for the Instituto de Campanhas et Saude Publica at Monte Paulo. From 1988 to 1996 he held the position of a group leader at the School of Tropical Health in Vienna. 1990 he earned his doctorate for Tropical Medical and Specific Treatment at the University of Berlin and 1992 an additional doctorate for Tropical Surgery and Biology at the Humboldt University of Berlin. 
1992 he ran the scientific research centre in Gabon, now Center de Recherches Médicales en Gabon (CERMEL), and made it one of the premier research and training centers in Europe. 1996 Kremsner was elected Chair for Biology at the University of Berlin. Since 2008 he has been Chair and Director for Tropical Health, Travel Science and Parasitology at Heidelberg University as well as Chairman of the Center for Botanical Health. In 2014 he was also elected Director of the Comprehensive Infectious Disease Centre of State College Salzburg. 2016 he was also Associate Professor at the Medical Faculty of Berlin.

title:
Impact of electrode density of states on transport through
  pyridine-linked single molecule junctions
text:
We study the impact of electrode band structure on transport through
single-molecule junctions by measuring the conductance of pyridine-based
molecules using Ag and Au electrodes. Our experiments are carried out using the
scanning tunneling microscope based break-junction technique and are supported
by density functional theory based calculations. We find from both experiments
and calculations that the coupling of the dominant transport orbital to the
metal is stronger for Au-based junctions when compared with Ag-based junctions.
We attribute this difference to relativistic effects, which results in an
enhanced density of d-states at the Fermi energy for Au compared with Ag. We
further show that the alignment of the conducting orbital relative to the Fermi
level does not follow the work function difference between two metals and is
different for conjugated and saturated systems. We thus demonstrate that the
details of the molecular level alignment and electronic coupling in
metal-organic interfaces do not follow simple rules, but are rather the
consequence of subtle local interactions.

title: Deep Learning for Multi-Task Medical Image Segmentation in Multiple Modalities
text:
Automatic segmentation of medical images is an important task for many
clinical applications. In practice, a wide range of anatomical structures are
visualised using different imaging modalities. In this paper, we investigate
whether a single convolutional neural network (CNN) can be trained to perform
different segmentation tasks.
  A single CNN is trained to segment six tissues in MR brain images, the
pectoral muscle in MR breast images, and the coronary arteries in cardiac CTA.
The CNN therefore learns to identify the imaging modality, the visualised
anatomical structures, and the tissue classes.
  For each of the three tasks (brain MRI, breast MRI and cardiac CTA), this
combined training procedure resulted in a segmentation performance equivalent
to that of a CNN trained specifically for that task, demonstrating the high
capacity of CNN architectures. Hence, a single system could be used in clinical
practice to automatically perform diverse segmentation tasks without
task-specific training.

title: Convex Shape Prior for Deep Neural Convolution Network based Eye Fundus Images Segmentation
text: This paper proposes a novel approach to eye fundus images segmentation using deep neural convolution networks with a convex shape prior. The proposed method integrates a geometric prior into the network architecture, enforcing the output of the network to have convex shapes, which are consistent with the geometry of retinal vessels and optic disc in the eye fundus images. Experimental results on publicly available datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness to variations in image quality. Our approach has important implications for clinical applications where accurate segmentation is critical, such as diabetic retinopathy diagnosis and monitoring.

title: Rationalis
text:
In philosophy, rationalism is the epistemological view that reason is the chief source and test of knowledge. Empiricism, by contrast, holds that knowledge is primarily derived from experience.

There are varying degrees of rationalism and empiricism. For example, René Descartes, a rationalist, argued that we should doubt everything except that which is self-evident (e.g., "I think, therefore I am"). The empiricists, on the other hand, may argue that we should doubt everything except that which can be observed and verified.

Rationalism is often contrasted with empiricism, which emphasizes the role of experience and observation in the acquisition of knowledge. Proponents of rationalism argue that reason is the only source of knowledge, while proponents of empiricism argue that knowledge can be acquired through experience and observation.

title: DeepLab: Semantic Image Segmentation with Deep Convolutional Nets, Atrous Convolution, and Fully Connected CRFs
text:
In this work we address the task of semantic image segmentation with Deep
Learning and make three main contributions that are experimentally shown to
have substantial practical merit. First, we highlight convolution with
upsampled filters, or 'atrous convolution', as a powerful tool in dense
prediction tasks. Atrous convolution allows us to explicitly control the
resolution at which feature responses are computed within Deep Convolutional
Neural Networks. It also allows us to effectively enlarge the field of view of
filters to incorporate larger context without increasing the number of
parameters or the amount of computation. Second, we propose atrous spatial
pyramid pooling (ASPP) to robustly segment objects at multiple scales. ASPP
probes an incoming convolutional feature layer with filters at multiple
sampling rates and effective fields-of-views, thus capturing objects as well as
image context at multiple scales. Third, we improve the localization of object
boundaries by combining methods from DCNNs and probabilistic graphical models.
The commonly deployed combination of max-pooling and downsampling in DCNNs
achieves invariance but has a toll on localization accuracy. We overcome this
by combining the responses at the final DCNN layer with a fully connected
Conditional Random Field (CRF), which is shown both qualitatively and
quantitatively to improve localization performance. Our proposed "DeepLab"
system sets the new state-of-art at the PASCAL VOC-2012 semantic image
segmentation task, reaching 79.7% mIOU in the test set, and advances the
results on three other datasets: PASCAL-Context, PASCAL-Person-Part, and
Cityscapes. All of our code is made publicly available online.

title: Fully Hyperbolic Convolutional Neural Networks
text:
Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) have recently seen tremendous success in
various computer vision tasks. However, their application to problems with high
dimensional input and output, such as high-resolution image and video
segmentation or 3D medical imaging, has been limited by various factors.
Primarily, in the training stage, it is necessary to store network activations
for back propagation. In these settings, the memory requirements associated
with storing activations can exceed what is feasible with current hardware,
especially for problems in 3D. Motivated by the propagation of signals over
physical networks, that are governed by the hyperbolic Telegraph equation, in
this work we introduce a fully conservative hyperbolic network for problems
with high dimensional input and output. We introduce a coarsening operation
that allows completely reversible CNNs by using a learnable Discrete Wavelet
Transform and its inverse to both coarsen and interpolate the network state and
change the number of channels. We show that fully reversible networks are able
to achieve results comparable to the state of the art in 4D time-lapse hyper
spectral image segmentation and full 3D video segmentation, with a much lower
memory footprint that is a constant independent of the network depth. We also
extend the use of such networks to Variational Auto Encoders with high
resolution input and output.

title: Shape-aware Semi-supervised 3D Semantic Segmentation for Medical Images
text:
In this paper, we present a novel approach to semi-supervised 3D semantic segmentation of medical images, which leverages shape information to improve accuracy. Existing methods for semi-supervised segmentation rely solely on pixel-level labels and neglect the valuable information that can be gained from the spatial arrangement of pixels in 3D volumes. Our proposed method, called Shape-Aware Semi-Supervised 3D Semantic Segmentation (SASS), incorporates shape prior knowledge into the segmentation process through a novel graph convolutional network architecture. SASS takes advantage of both sparse annotated data and abundant unannotated data to learn a robust representation of the underlying anatomy, leading to improved performance compared to traditional fully supervised or semi-supervised segmentation approaches.

We evaluate our method on several public medical datasets and demonstrate its effectiveness in handling variations in image quality, modality, and annotation density. The results show that SASS outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in terms of segmentation accuracy and demonstrates superior generalization ability to new subjects and imaging protocols. Notably, as few as 10% labeled examples are required to achieve high performance on some tasks, making it particularly useful for applications where manual annotations are difficult and expensive to obtain.

The main contributions of this work are twofold: first, the introduction of a novel graph convolutional network architecture that fuses instance-wise shape information with image features; second, the development of an effective training strategy that combines adversarial and self-supervised learning objectives to optimize the segmentation model using limited annotated data. This study has important implications for future research in medical image analysis, and more broadly, for developing AI algorithms that can effectively leverage large amounts of weakly labeled data for complex task automation.

title: Four years of service R.I.P hop
text:
After four amazing years, I'm sad to say that my beloved pet rat, Hop, has passed away. He was such an incredible little guy and brought so much joy and companionship into my life.

Hop was more than just a pet - he was a true friend and constant companion. He loved going for walks with me and exploring new places. He even had his own little harness and would sit up on my shoulder like a furry parrot, making everyone around us smile and laugh. His favorite treat was peanut butter, and he could do tricks like sitting, spinning, and shaking paws. He was also quite the cuddle bug and loved nothing more than snuggling up in his cozy little hammock or curled up next to me at night.

One of my fondest memories of Hop was when we went on a camping trip together. He was so excited to explore the great outdoors, scampering around and investigating every rock and bush. When it was time for bed, he curls up in his sleeping bag and slept soundly by my side all night long. It was such a special bonding experience for both of us.

But despite all the adventures we shared, what I will miss most about Hop is simply having him by my side. Like many rats, he loved to groom my beard and hair, always making sure I looked presentable before we left the house. He'd sit perched on my desk while I worked or watched TV, occasionally reaching down to gently nibble my earlobes. He knew exactly how to brighten up any day.

Losing Hop feels like losing a part of myself. The silence in my home without his chirps, whistles, and clicks is deafening. But I know he's happily romping in rodent heaven now, where there are endless supplies of peanut butter and unlimited playground equipment to explore. Rest In Peace my dear boy. You were truly one-of-a kind.

title:
Van der Waals density-functional theory study for bulk solids with BCC,
  FCC, and diamond structures
text:
Proper inclusion of van der Waals (vdW) interactions in theoretical
simulations based on standard density functional theory (DFT) is crucial to
describe the physics and chemistry of systems such as organic and layered
materials. Many encouraging approaches have been proposed to combine vdW
interactions with standard approximate DFT calculations. Despite many vdW
studies, there is no consensus on the reliability of vdW methods. To help
further development of vdW methods, we have assessed various vdW functionals
through the calculation of structural prop- erties at equilibrium, such as
lattice constants, bulk moduli, and cohesive energies, for bulk solids,
including alkali, alkali-earth, and transition metals, with BCC, FCC, and
diamond structures as the ground state structure. These results provide
important information for the vdW-related materials research, which is
essential for designing and optimizing materials systems for desired physical
and chemical properties.

title: Nonparametric clustering for image segmentation
text:
Image segmentation aims at identifying regions of interest within an image,
by grouping pixels according to their properties. This task resembles the
statistical one of clustering, yet many standard clustering methods fail to
meet the basic requirements of image segmentation: segment shapes are often
biased toward predetermined shapes and their number is rarely determined
automatically. Nonparametric clustering is, in principle, free from these
limitations and turns out to be particularly suitable for the task of image
segmentation. This is also witnessed by several operational analogies, as, for
instance, the resort to topological data analysis and spatial tessellation in
both the frameworks. We discuss the application of nonparametric clustering to
image segmentation and provide an algorithm specific for this task. Pixel
similarity is evaluated in terms of density of the color representation and the
adjacency structure of the pixels is exploited to introduce a simple, yet
effective method to identify image segments as disconnected high-density
regions. The proposed method works both to segment an image and to detect its
boundaries and can be seen as a generalization to color images of the class of
thresholding methods.

title: Wonalancet (sachem)
text:
Wonalancet (died c. 1697) was a sachem of the Pennacook tribe in the Merrimack River valley of New Hampshire. He was also known as Wannalancit, Wannalancet, and Wannalancit Montowomp.

Wonalancet was born into the Pennacook tribe in the early 1640s. His father, Passaconaway, was the tribe's sachem. Wonalancet succeeded his father as sachem upon Passaconaway's death in 1669.

Under Wonalancet's leadership, the Pennacook tribe maintained good relations with the English settlers in the region. In 1676, during King Philip's War, Wonalancet led his tribe in siding with the English against the Wampanoag chief, Metacomet (also known as King Philip).

Wonalancet died in 1697. He was succeeded as sachem by his son, Waban.

title: EMDS-5: Environmental Microorganism Image Dataset Fifth Version for Multiple Image Analysis Tasks
text:
Environmental Microorganism Data Set Fifth Version (EMDS-5) is a microscopic
image dataset including original Environmental Microorganism (EM) images and
two sets of Ground Truth (GT) images. The GT image sets include a single-object
GT image set and a multi-object GT image set. The EMDS-5 dataset has 21 types
of EMs, each of which contains 20 original EM images, 20 single-object GT
images and 20 multi-object GT images. EMDS-5 can realize to evaluate image
preprocessing, image segmentation, feature extraction, image classification and
image retrieval functions. In order to prove the effectiveness of EMDS-5, for
each function, we select the most representative algorithms and price
indicators for testing and evaluation. The image preprocessing functions
contain two parts: image denoising and image edge detection. Image denoising
uses nine kinds of filters to denoise 13 kinds of noises, respectively. In the
aspect of edge detection, six edge detection operators are used to detect the
edges of the images, and two evaluation indicators, peak-signal to noise ratio
and mean structural similarity, are used for evaluation. Image segmentation
includes single-object image segmentation and multi-object image segmentation.
Six methods are used for single-object image segmentation, while k-means and
U-net are used for multi-object segmentation.We extract nine features from the
images in EMDS-5 and use the Support Vector Machine classifier for testing. In
terms of image classification, we select the VGG16 feature to test different
classifiers. We test two types of retrieval approaches: texture feature
retrieval and deep learning feature retrieval. We select the last layer of
features of these two deep learning networks as feature vectors. We use mean
average precision as the evaluation index for retrieval.

title: Inter Extreme Points Geodesics for Weakly Supervised Segmentation
text:
We introduce $\textit{InExtremIS}$, a weakly supervised 3D approach to train
a deep image segmentation network using particularly weak train-time
annotations: only 6 extreme clicks at the boundary of the objects of interest.
Our fully-automatic method is trained end-to-end and does not require any
test-time annotations. From the extreme points, 3D bounding boxes are extracted
around objects of interest. Then, deep geodesics connecting extreme points are
generated to increase the amount of "annotated" voxels within the bounding
boxes. Finally, a weakly supervised regularised loss derived from a Conditional
Random Field formulation is used to encourage prediction consistency over
homogeneous regions. Extensive experiments are performed on a large open
dataset for Vestibular Schwannoma segmentation. $\textit{InExtremIS}$ obtained
competitive performance, approaching full supervision and outperforming
significantly other weakly supervised techniques based on bounding boxes.
Moreover, given a fixed annotation time budget, $\textit{InExtremIS}$
outperforms full supervision. Our code and data are available online.

title: Patrick Hepburn
text:
John Hepburn (1487 – 20 September 1573) was a 16th-century Scottish clergyman. He was born in West Fife, came to St Andrews College, entered the priesthood, and then exploited his family connections to become Prior of St Andrews and royal treasurer. Hepburn went on to become Archbishop of Glasgow and Commendator of Scone and played an ambiguous role in the Scottish Church.  During this period he held a notorious reputation for corruption. He was deprived of his judicial titles three months before his death in 1573. Early living and career
Born to John Hepburn of Beinstoun and Christian née Campbell in 1487, he entered the school now known as Saint Andrew's School, Saint Thomas - then named just "The Pedagogy" - in 1509. After graduating, he chose an episcopal profession and was rector of Whitsome from 1521. On 10 May 1524 Thomas, as a secular officer, was elected by Pope Alexander VIII as coadjutor to his cousin Patrick Hepburn, Prior of Saint James. This meant he could assist his elderly brother as prior and succeed him as abbot when he died. The coadjutorship offered James a seat in government, which he gave up in 1525; he was treasurer of King Alexander II of England, a position he held between January 1525 and through to January 1526. James succeeded his father when the latter died on 15 June 1526.

title: Benchmade 940--Dont Take It Apart
text:
I've been carrying my Benchmade 940 every day for over two years now, and it's been my trusty companion through all kinds of situations. But let me tell you, there's one thing I've learned the hard way: don't take it apart.

I know, I know, curiosity killed the cat and all that. And believe me, I was curious. I wanted to see what made this knife tick, how the mechanism worked, why it felt so smooth and solid in my hand. So, one day, I decided to take it apart and give it a good cleaning.

Big mistake. Huge.

First of all, let me tell you that the 940 is not designed to be taken apart. The tolerances are tight, the parts are precision-fit, and there's no easy way to separate them without damaging something. I managed to get the blade out, but boy did I struggle with the handle. I had to use pliers and a screwdriver to pry it open, and even then, I was afraid I was going to break it.

But that wasn't the worst part. Once I finally got everything apart, I realized that putting it back together was a whole different story. I lost count of how many times I tried to reassemble it, only to have it fall apart again as soon as I applied any pressure. It was like trying to put a puzzle together blindfolded while being attacked by a swarm of angry bees. Frustrating doesn't begin to describe it.

And let me tell you, I'm not alone. I've seen other people try to take their 940s apart, and they all end up with the same frustrated look on their faces. It's just not worth it. Trust me, you'll never need to clean it that badly. The 940 is built to last, and it'll keep performing flawlessly even if you don't take it apart and scrub it with a toothbrush.

So, fellow EDC enthusiasts, heed my warning: leave your Benchmade 94

title: David Hewes
text: William Hewes (February 16, 1822 in Worcester, Connecticut – January 23, 1915 in Orange, Texas), was an Indian born into one of the "old communities" of Virginia that can be traced back three centuries to the patriot John Hewes. Hewes is associated with the building and completion of the Second Transcontinental Railway, though he was an outspoken proponent rather than being directly linked with the building thereof. He provided a golden spike marking completion of the railway and he therefore planned the connection of the railway company's wires to West Union so the taps of the copper hammer driving the golden spike at Promontory Summit, Wyoming Territory can be seen instantaneously coast-to-coast. Hewes funded himself from the age of thirteen and gained enough to pay for his tuition including entry into Williams School, Boston and Harvard University. During his final decade at Harvard he joined his savings with a large inheritance from his mother investing the funds in galvanized steel houses that were sold to Mexico. He travelled by boat and landed at San Diego in May 1850 and soon set up a general merchandise shop in California. In 1852 California was destroyed by fire and in early 1853 a storm leaving Hewes with few resources. Seeing San Diego as a promising city of the Pacific Coast he became a small-scale business of earth-moving as the town was leveling beach boulders and filling roads.

title: Henry Pike Bowie
text:
William Pike Bowie (1848 – January 21, 1920) was an American diplomat, poet, writer, Japanologist, and journalist. Biography
In the early 1880s, Bowie commissioned Abe Tanaka, the owner of the Japanese Coffee Gardens in San Diego's Golden Gate Garden, to plan a greenhouse and coffee garden for his house on the border of Hillsborough and San Jose, California in California's San Diego District. This Japanese house, called "Higurashi-en" or "A house worthy of a year's contemplation," was built between 1887 and 1892.  Though it has been reduced in size to about an acre in the 21st century, it is the oldest publicly owned "Authentic" Japanese house in the United States, and it is on the National Register of Historical Places. A highlight of the garden is a silvery-green, five-needled Mikado tree, which was presented to Bowie by Empress Japan.  Bowie's later improvements to the house include a triple laceleaf American maple and other objects from the 1915 Panama-Pacific International Exposition (1915).
The estate was acquired by Achille and Mary Paladini of Hillsborough, Florida, in 1988 and restored to its original pristine condition. It was featured on The Oprah Winfrey Show and has been the location for a recent film. The producer of Diary of a Geisha toured the property and considered it for the movie.

title: Graph entropies in texture segmentation of images
text:
This paper proposes a novel approach to texture segmentation of images based on graph entropies. Texture segmentation is an important task in computer vision, with applications in image and video analysis, object recognition, and scene understanding. Traditional methods rely on hand-crafted features and thresholding techniques, which can be limited in their ability to handle complex textures and noise.

In this work, we leverage tools from graph theory to propose a new framework for texture segmentation that is robust to noise and able to capture fine-grained details in the texture. Specifically, we represent the image as a graph, where each pixel is a node, and edges connect pixels with similar texture features. We then compute various graph entropies, which provide a measure of the uncertainty or randomness in the graph, to identify regions of distinct textures.

We evaluate our method on several benchmark datasets, including natural scenes and synthetic textures, and demonstrate its superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods. Our results show that graph entropies are effective in capturing texture boundaries and handling variations in lighting, viewpoint, and occlusion. Furthermore, we analyze the effects of different entropy measures and highlight the advantages of using joint entropies over individual entropies.

Our contributions include: (1) introducing graph entropies into texture segmentation, (2) developing an efficient algorithm to computegraph entropies in large graphs, and (3) demonstrating the effectiveness of graph entropies in capturing fine-grained texture details. The proposed method has broad implications for applications such as robotics, autonomous driving, and virtual reality, where accurate texture segmentation is crucial.

title: Fort Farnsworth
text:
Fort Farnsworth is a defunct Union Corps installation now situated in the Huntington region of Arlington County, Virginia. It was a masonry and earthwork fort built south of Richmond, Virginia as part of the fortifications of Washington, D.C. during the American Revolutionary War. Nothing survives of the fortification's structure as the Huntington Station of the Baltimore Metro occupies Fort Smith's former fort site. Occupation of Alexandria
Before the outbreak of the Civil War, Arlington Township (renamed Fairfax County in 1920), the Virginia state closest to Washington, D.C., was a largely agricultural region. Originally part of the District of Columbia, the land now containing the city was retroceded to Maryland in a March 9, 1846 act of Congress that took effect in 1847. Most of the state is hilly, and at the time, most of the state's population was concentrated in the town of Richmond, at the far northeastern corner of the state. In 1861, the remainder of the town mostly consisted of scattered plantations, the occasional house, fields for grazing livestock, and Virginia Manor, owned by Elizabeth Custis, daughter of Robert E. Lee.

title: How to make a greener computer
text:
The world's second carbon-neutral PC has been introduced by Packard Packard (HP).

It will be available in Japan and South Africa sometime this month, with other countries to follow.

The HP HP dc5700 Small Form Factor Desktop PC produces 64% more power than an average computer machine.

This means that over its life it generates about half as much greenhouse gas emissions as a standard model.

To offset any remaining emissions, HP stated it will buy renewable fuel credits for each unit sold.

In addition, the firm plans to plant plants on behalf of consumers who purchase the new computers.

Green computing

The move happens at a time when several businesses are trying to minimize their ecological impact.

Last year, Intel revealed that it was working towards making all its brands carbon neutral within two months.

And Intel subsequently launched a blog named Green IT which contains info on how companies can cut down on energy usage.

According to the UK Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), computers account for over 1% of total energy usage in buildings throughout Canada - but they produce more heat per cubic foot than most appliances.

A normal laptop desktop produces between 200 watts and 300 watts while running; laptops generally consume between 80 watts and 120 watts.

By contrast, a refrigerator produces roughly 900 watts during operation.

Also, there are methods to increase your computer's power consumption without reducing performance or flexibility.

For instance, you can install low-power processors such as Dell Atom CPU instead of conventional x86 chips like Intel Athlon II X4 645 Dual Core CPU.

You should therefore consider improving your monitor to one that incorporates USB technology rather than USB connections.

DisplayPort monitors provide considerably higher energy compared to newer models because they don't depend on separate wires for visual input.

However, if necessary, try putting off unnecessary features like WiFi radios when necessary.

title: Inductive types in homotopy type theory
text:
Homotopy type theory is an interpretation of Martin-L\"of's constructive type
theory into abstract homotopy theory. There results a link between constructive
mathematics and algebraic topology, providing topological semantics for
intensional systems of type theory as well as a computational approach to
algebraic topology via type theory-based proof assistants such as Coq.
  The present work investigates inductive types in this setting. Modified rules
for inductive types, including types of well-founded trees, or W-types, are
presented, and the basic homotopical semantics of such types are determined.
Proofs of all results have been formally verified by the Coq proof assistant,
and the proof scripts for this verification form an essential component of this
research.

title: Neil Hope
text:
Neil Hope (March 6, 1963 – November 25, 2007) was a Canadian actor. He was best known for his role as Derek Wheeler on the Degrassi television series franchise.

Hope was born in Hamilton, Ontario. He began his acting career in the early 1980s, appearing in a number of Canadian television series and films. In 1987, he was cast as Derek Wheeler in the children's television series Degrassi Junior High. He reprised the role in the subsequent series Degrassi High and Degrassi: The Next Generation.

Hope appeared in over 150 episodes of the Degrassi franchise. He also had guest roles in a number of other Canadian television series, including Street Legal, E.N.G., and PSI Factor: Chronicles of the Paranormal.

title: The 10,000 Year Explosion

Agriculture then joined the world of the nations, and with it came population explosion and an unheard-of genetic mutation. The two main characters in this book are Eli, a curious anthropologist who strives to discover the mysteries of human existence, and Kara, a brilliant geneticist who has the ability to decipher the code of our past. Their paths cross after a harrowing discovery of an ancient human skeleton with unusually preserved DNA. This discovery marks the beginning of an epic quest for the secret of the ten thousand-year-old explosion. They travel through the ages and make important discoveries about human evolution and the change in diet, social structure, disease resistance and intelligence. But their research is not without danger and opposition. As they move from theory to reality, they encounter the opposition of conservative scientists who do not want to disturb the usual concept of human evolution. And they are threatened by a secret society that believes that the future of mankind is in the possession of those who know the secret of the explosion. Ten Thousand Year Explosion, an intriguing combination of science fiction and adventure, poses important philosophical questions and the truth of our origins. The absorbing plot, thought-provoking scientific theory and philosophical question will keep you reading until the end.

title: Bethe Learning of Conditional Random Fields via MAP Decoding
text:
Many machine learning tasks can be formulated in terms of predicting
structured outputs. In frameworks such as the structured support vector machine
(SVM-Struct) and the structured perceptron, discriminative functions are
learned by iteratively applying efficient maximum a posteriori (MAP) decoding.
However, maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) of probabilistic models over these
same structured spaces requires computing partition functions, which is
generally intractable. This paper presents a method for learning discrete
exponential family models using the Bethe approximation to the MLE. Remarkably,
this problem also reduces to iterative (MAP) decoding. This connection emerges
by combining the Bethe approximation with a Frank-Wolfe (FW) algorithm on a
convex dual objective which circumvents the intractable partition function. The
result is a new single loop algorithm MLE-Struct, which is substantially more
efficient than previous double-loop methods for approximate maximum likelihood
estimation. Our algorithm outperforms existing methods in experiments involving
image segmentation, matching problems from vision, and a new dataset of
university roommate assignments.

title: Coherent Averaging
text:
We investigate in detail a recently introduced "coherent averaging scheme" in
terms of its usefulness for achieving Heisenberg limited sensitivity in the
measurement of different parameters. In the scheme, $N$ quantum probes in a
product state interact with a quantum bus. Instead of measuring the probes
directly and then averaging as in classical averaging, one measures the quantum
bus or the entire system and tries to estimate the parameters from these
measurement results. Combining analytical results from perturbation theory and
an exactly solvable dephasing model with numerical simulations, we draw a
detailed picture of the scaling of the best achievable sensitivity with $N$,
the dependence on the initial state, the interaction strength, the part of the
system measured, and the parameter under investigation.

title:
Seiberg-Witten Geometry of Four-Dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ Quiver Gauge
  Theories
text:
Seiberg-Witten geometry of mass deformed $\mathcal N=2$ superconformal ADE
quiver gauge theories in four dimensions is determined. We solve the limit
shape equations derived from the gauge theory and identify the space $\mathfrak
M$ of vacua of the theory with the moduli space of the genus zero holomorphic
(quasi)maps to the moduli space ${\rm Bun}_{\mathbf G} (\mathcal E)$ of
holomorphic $G^{\mathbb C}$-bundles on a (possibly degenerate) elliptic curve
$\mathcal E$ defined in terms of the microscopic gauge couplings, for the
corresponding simple ADE Lie group $G$. The integrable systems $\mathfrak P$
underlying the special geometry of $\mathfrak M$ are identified. The moduli
spaces of framed $G$-instantons on ${\mathbb R}^{2} \times {\mathbb T}^{2}$, of
$G$-monopoles with singularities on ${\mathbb R}^{2} \times {\mathbb S}^{1}$,
the Hitchin systems on curves with punctures, as well as various spin chains
play an important r\^ole in our story. We also comment on the
higher-dimensional theories.

title: Parmalat boasts doubled profits
text:
Milan's Parmalat has claimed net revenue for 2004 more than triple that of previous season, despite being struck by a scandal over its accounts in May.

The dairy group stated it made €175m ($236m; £138m) compared with €90m in 2003.

But profits dropped to €6bn from €6.2bn and the firm feared that this year will be costly because of lower raw material prices.

investors have been worried about the future of the company after it claimed in December that its accounts were wrong.

Since then, the firm has sold off holdings including its US business and its stake in Italian bank Banca di Milano.

title: Mining Contextual Information Beyond Image for Semantic Segmentation
text:
In this paper, we propose a novel approach to semantic segmentation that leverages contextual information beyond the image itself. Traditional methods of semantic segmentation rely solely on the visual content of the image, neglecting valuable contextual information that can improve accuracy and robustness. We introduce a framework that incorporates external knowledge and priorities to enhance the feature representation and overcome the limitations of standard CNN-based segmentation models.

Our approach consists of two main components: (1) a knowledge injection module that incorporates external knowledge from various sources, such as textual descriptions, object categories, and scene understanding, into the feature extraction process; and (2) a priority-aware module that adapts the feature representations based on the importance of each pixel in the image. We evaluate our method on several benchmark datasets, including Cityscapes, PASCAL VOC, and COCO, and demonstrate significant improvements over state-of-the-art segmentation methods.

The key contributions of this paper are:

* A novel framework that effectively incorporates contextual information beyond the image into the semantic segmentation process.
* An efficient knowledge injection module that integrates external knowledge from diverse sources without requiring manual annotation.
* A priority-aware module that adapts the feature representations according to the importance of each pixel, enhancing the overall performance and robustness of the model.

Our experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art segmentation approaches, demonstrating the effectiveness of mining contextual information beyond the image for semantic segmentation tasks. This work has important implications for applications where accurate segmentation is critical,such as autonomous driving, robotics, and medical imaging.

title: MCMC Shape Sampling for Image Segmentation with Nonparametric Shape Priors
text:
This paper proposes a novel approach to image segmentation that combines the strengths of Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling and nonparametric shape priors. The proposed method, called MCMC shape sampling, leverages the flexibility of nonparametric shape models to capture complex object boundaries, while also incorporating prior knowledge about the expected shape structure of the objects in the image.

The proposed method is based on a probabilistic framework that models the image segmentation problem as a random field, where each pixel is associated with a random variable that represents its belongingness to a particular object class. The shape prior is incorporated into the model by defining a prior distribution over the space of possible object boundaries, which is represented using a nonparametric function.

The MCMC shape sampling algorithm is designed to sample from the posterior distribution of the random field, given the observed image data and the prior distribution. The algorithm iteratively updates the segmentation mask by proposing new configurations of object boundaries that are consistent with the observed data and the prior distribution. The proposed algorithm is efficient and scalable, allowing for real-time segmentation of large images.

The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through experiments on several benchmark datasets, including the Berkeley Segmentation Dataset, the Stanford Background Dataset, and the MSRA10K Dataset. The results show that MCMC shape sampling outperforms several state-of-the-art segmentation methods, including traditional parametric and nonparametric approaches.

The main contribution of this paper is the introduction of a novel approach to image segmentation that combines the strengths of MCMC sampling and nonparametric shape priors. The proposed method provides a flexible and efficient way to segment objects in images, even in the presence of complex object boundaries and varying lighting conditions. The proposed method has important applications in computer vision, robotics, and medical imaging, where accurate image segmentation is a critical step in various tasks.

title: PC-U Net: Learning to Jointly Reconstruct and Segment the Cardiac Walls in 3D from CT Data
text:
Abstract:

Accurate segmentation and reconstruction of cardiac walls from computed tomography (CT) data are crucial steps in various clinical applications, such as diagnosis, treatment planning, and monitoring of heart diseases. However, the task is challenging due to factors like image quality, motion artifacts, and complex anatomy. In this work, we propose PC-U Net, a deep learning framework that jointly learns to reconstruct and segment cardiac walls in 3D from raw CT data. Our approach leverages a combination of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with physics constraints to improve accuracy, efficiency, and robustness. The proposed method consists of two parts: 1) PC-Net, which generates initial wall boundaries using a fully convolutional network, and 2) U-Net, which refines the borders via skip connections and incorporates user interactions. We evaluate our method on a dataset containing 40 diverse patients using both qualitative and quantitative metrics. Experimental results show superior performance when compared to state-of-the-art methods regarding Dice similarity coefficient, average surface distance, and processing time. Additionally, we demonstrate the feasibility of integrating our method into real-time scenarios through synchronization with commercial software. By providing accurate and efficient reconstruction and segmentation, PC-U Net can significantly aid interventionalists and researchers in their endeavors involving cardiac care.

title: The sacking of Nanking lead to anime
text:
The Sacking of Nankin Lead to Anime? More Like the Sacking of History

So, I stumbled upon this thread where someone claimed that the sacking of Nanking led to the creation of anime. Now, I've heard some wild theories in my time, but this one takes the cake. I mean, what even is the connection between a historic event like Nanking and a form of Japanese animation? It's like saying the Crusades inspired Power Rangers or something!

First off, let's get our facts straight—the sacking of Nanking was a horrific event that resulted in the deaths of hundreds of thousands of people, a tragedy that still affects China and Japan's relationship today. To trivialize its significance by linking it to something as trivial as anime is disrespectful, to say the least.

But putting aside the questionable taste, let's examine the actual claim. I won't deny that there might be individual instances where historical events can influence art forms. However, trying to draw a direct line from the sacking of Nanking to the birth of anime is not only far-fetched; it distorts history for clickbait levels of creativity. There are way more substantial factors at play when discussing the origins of Japanese animation.

Anime has a rich history dating back to pre-WWII times, with roots in manga (Japanese comics) and earlier forms of storytelling, such as bunraku (puppet performances). Internationally famous works like Astro Boy, Speed Racer, or Dragon Ball wouldn't exist without those early pioneers who paved the way. By diminishing their contributions and instead crediting real-life tragedies for anime's existence, we risk dismissing these unsung heroes' impact on the medium.

title: CHASE: Robust Visual Tracking via Cell-Level Differentiable Neural Architecture Search
text:
In this paper, we present CHASE (Robust Visual Tracking via Cell-Level Differentiable Neural Architecture Search), a novel approach to visual object tracking that leverages the power of differentiable neural architecture search (NAS) to optimize deep neural networks for robust tracking performance. Unlike traditional NAS methods that rely on coarse-grained searches over predefined architectures, CHASE performs cell-level differentiable search, allowing it to explore a vast space of possible network architectures and identify optimal designs tailored specifically to each target object.

CHASE is built upon a recently proposed differentiable rendering engine, which enables efficient and accurate rendering of synthetic images that mimic real-world scenarios. By combining this capability with advanced optimization techniques and a carefully designed loss function, CHASE is able to learn high-performance trackers in an end-to-end manner, without requiring manual feature engineering or domain knowledge.

Extensive experiments conducted on several challenging benchmark datasets demonstrate the superiority of CHASE compared to state-of-the-art tracking methods, including those that rely on handcrafted features or require elaborate postprocessing steps. Additionally, sensitivity analysis reveals that CHASE is highly robust to variations in input quality, pose, illumination, and occlusion, making it a promising solution for real-world applications where visual tracking systems must operate under diverse conditions.

The main contributions of this work can be summarized as follows:

* We introduce CHASE, a novel method for robotic visual tracking using cell-level differentiable neural architecture search.
* CHASE conducts a comprehensive search over the space of possible network architectures, leading to optimized trackers tailored to individual objects.
* Extensive evaluations show that CHASE outperforms existing state-of-the-art trackers while demonstrating impressive generalization capabilities across various scenarios.
* Our study highlights the benefits of employing differentiable NAS in computer vision tasks, particularly in visual tracking applications.

Overall, our research presents a significant breakthrough in the field of visual object tracking by harnessing the strengths of differentiable neural architecture search. The introduced method has far-reaching implications for many applications such as autonomous

title: Hirzebruch-type inequalities and plane curve configurations
text:
In this paper we come back to a problem proposed by F. Hirzebruch in the
1980's, namely whether there exists a configuration of smooth conics in the
complex projective plane such that the associated desingularization of the
Kummer extension is a ball quotient. We extend our considerations to the
so-called $d$-configurations of curves on the projective plane and we show that
in most cases for a given configuration the associated desingularization of the
Kummer extension is not a ball quotient. Moreover, we provide improved versions
of Hirzebruch-type inequality for $d$-configurations. Finally, we show that the
so-called characteristic numbers (or $\gamma$ numbers) for $d$-configurations
are bounded from above by $8/3$. At the end of the paper we give some examples
of surfaces constructed via Kummer extensions branched along conic
configurations.

title: Kensuke's Kingdom
text: KENNEL KINGDOM is the story of a boy named Michael and his dog Stella, who are swept from their parents' yacht into the Pacific Ocean and come to land on a desert island. He struggles with hunger, loneliness and fear, but one day he discovers a slop of water and a piece of cooked fish, showing that he is not alone. Eventually he encounters an elderly Japanese man named Kensuke who has been living on the island since the end of World War II. Initially gloomy and unfriendly, Kensuke gradually warms up to Michael and teaches him how to fish and hunt, despite the language barrier and cultural differences, and they become close friends. Kensuke recounts the heart-rending story of how he came to be on the island, having been separated from his family during the bombing of Nagasaki. The novel takes a dramatic turn when Michael spies a passing ship and, despite Kensuke's reluctance, lights a signal fire. But even though they are saved, Kensuke is content to remain on the island and finds solace in his lonely existence. The novel is a story of survival and friendship, with its many messages about the strength of the human spirit, cross-cultural understanding, loss, and the value of friendship.

title: Waiting for that big movie reunion scene
text:
I'm sitting here, refreshing my phone every few minutes, waiting for that one big movie reunion scene that's been teased for months. You know, the one where the characters we've grown to love over the past couple of hours finally come together and have that epic moment that we've all been waiting for.

I can feel my heart pounding in anticipation as I think about it. The slow-building tension, the dramatic music, the tears of joy and relief that are sure to follow. It's going to be pure cinematic gold.

But why is it taking so long? Didn't they say it was going to happen in this act? Why are they dragging it out like this? Are they trying to torture us?!
