title: Incorporating prior knowledge in medical image segmentation: a survey
text:
In recent years, machine learning has revolutionized the field of medical image segmentation by enabling accurate and automated identifier of anatomical structures and diseased tissues. However, the success of these algorithms heavily relies on large amounts of annotated data, which are time-consuming and expensive to create. One way to overcome this limitation is incorporating prior knowledge into the segmentation process.

This survey provides thorough overview of techniques used for incorporating prior knowledge into deep learning models for medical image segmentation. We discuss various sources of prior knowledge, including expert knowledge, transfer learning, multi-modal imaging, and graph-based methods. Moreover, we delve into different strategies for integrating this knowledge, such as pre-processing techniques, feature engineering, loss functions, and ensemble learning. Finally, we highlight the challenges associated with using prior knowledge in medical image segmentation and identify future research directions in this area.

The main contribution of our work lies in providing a comprehensive overview of strategies for incorporating prior knowledge in medical image segmentation tasks using deep learning models. Our findings demonstrate that effectively leveraging prior knowledge can significantly improve segmentation performance, reduce the need for annotated training data, and enable more robust generalization across populations and datasets.

title: Splenomegaly Segmentation using Global Convolutional Kernels and Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks
text:
Spleen volume estimation using automated image segmentation technique may be
used to detect splenomegaly (abnormally enlarged spleen) on Magnetic Resonance
Imaging (MRI) scans. In recent years, Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (DCNN)
segmentation methods have demonstrated advantages for abdominal organ
segmentation. However, variations in both size and shape of the spleen on MRI
images may result in large false positive and false negative labeling when
deploying DCNN based methods. In this paper, we propose the Splenomegaly
Segmentation Network (SSNet) to address spatial variations when segmenting
extraordinarily large spleens. SSNet was designed based on the framework of
image-to-image conditional generative adversarial networks (cGAN).
Specifically, the Global Convolutional Network (GCN) was used as the generator
to reduce false negatives, while the Markovian discriminator (PatchGAN) was
used to alleviate false positives. A cohort of clinically acquired 3D MRI scans
(both T1 weighted and T2 weighted) from patients with splenomegaly were used to
train and test the networks. The experimental results demonstrated that a mean
Dice coefficient of 0.9260 and a median Dice coefficient of 0.9262 using SSNet
on independently tested MRI volumes of patients with splenomegaly.

title: Learning-Based Cost Functions for 3D and 4D Multi-Surface Multi-Object Segmentation of Knee MRI: Data from the Osteoarthritis Initiative
text:
This paper proposes a novel approach to 3D and 4D multi-surface multi-object segmentation of knee MRI data using learning-based cost functions. The proposed method leverages the large-scale Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI) dataset, which provides a unique opportunity to study knee osteoarthritis and related conditions.

Existing methods for segmenting knee MRI data often rely on hand-crafted features and manual parameter tuning, which can be time-consuming and suboptimal. In contrast, our approach uses learning-based cost functions to automatically learn discriminative features and optimize segmentation parameters. This allows for more accurate and efficient segmentation of knee MRI data, which is critical for clinical applications such as disease diagnosis and treatment planning.

Our proposed method consists of two main components: a feature extraction module and a segmentation module. The feature extraction module uses a combination of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and spatial pyramid pooling to extract discriminative features from the MRI data. The segmentation module then uses a probabilistic graphical model to jointly segment the multiple surfaces and objects in the knee joint, including bones, cartilage, and soft tissue.

We evaluate our method on a large dataset of knee MRI scans from the OAI, and compare it to state-of-the-art methods. Our results show that our method outperforms existing approaches in terms of segmentation accuracy and efficiency. We also demonstrate the clinical relevance of our method by applying it to a subset of patients with knee osteoarthritis, and show that it can accurately identify and quantify the extent of cartilage damage and bone marrow lesions.

title: Motorsport in India
text:
Motorsport in India is currently governed by the Federation of Motor Sports Clubs of India (FMSCI). FMSCI is affiliated to the Federation Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA), the world body for motorsport.

The first motor race in India was held in Madras (now Chennai) in Dec 1904. The race was organised by the Madras Automobile Club and was held on a beach. This was followed by a race from Bombay to Poona in 1908.

The first formal motor racing event was held in Sholavandan, near Madurai, in Feb 1935. This race was organised by the South India Racing Association. The Madras Motor Race was held annually from 1936 onwards on a sand track laid out at Chennai beach.

The first National Racing Championship was held in 1954. This was followed by the setting up of the National Racing Championship for production cars in 1955.

There are currently three National Championships - Indian National Rally Championship, Indian National Racing Championship and Indian National Drag Racing Championship.

There are also several state level championships held throughout the year.

title: Medical Image Segmentation Based on Multi-Modal Convolutional Neural Network: Study on Image Fusion Schemes
text:
Image analysis using more than one modality (i.e. multi-modal) has been
increasingly applied in the field of biomedical imaging. One of the challenges
in performing the multimodal analysis is that there exist multiple schemes for
fusing the information from different modalities, where such schemes are
application-dependent and lack a unified framework to guide their designs. In
this work we firstly propose a conceptual architecture for the image fusion
schemes in supervised biomedical image analysis: fusing at the feature level,
fusing at the classifier level, and fusing at the decision-making level.
Further, motivated by the recent success in applying deep learning for natural
image analysis, we implement the three image fusion schemes above based on the
Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with varied structures, and combined into a
single framework. The proposed image segmentation framework is capable of
analyzing the multi-modality images using different fusing schemes
simultaneously. The framework is applied to detect the presence of soft tissue
sarcoma from the combination of Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), Computed
Tomography (CT) and Positron Emission Tomography (PET) images. It is found from
the results that while all the fusion schemes outperform the single-modality
schemes, fusing at the feature level can generally achieve the best performance
in terms of both accuracy and computational cost, but also suffers from the
decreased robustness in the presence of large errors in any image modalities.

title: Iris Recognition with a Database of Iris Images Obtained in Visible Light Using Smartphone Camera
text:
This paper presents a novel approach for iris recognition using a database of iris images obtained in visible light using a smartphone camera. Existing iris recognition systems rely on specialized cameras and controlled lighting conditions, which can be expensive and limit their practicality. In contrast, our approach utilizes the ubiquitous smartphone camera and visible light, making it more accessible and cost-effective.

We propose a two-stage framework that consists of image preprocessing and feature extraction, followed by matching and recognition. In the first stage, we apply a series of image processing techniques to enhance the quality of the captured iris images and remove artifacts. In the second stage, we extract discriminative features from the preprocessed images using a combination of local binary patterns and Gabor filters.

We evaluate the performance of our approach using a dataset of 1000 iris images captured in visible light using a smartphone camera. Our results show that our approach achieves an accuracy of 95.1%, outperforming existing methods that use similar hardware. We also perform a series of experiments to analyze the effectiveness of our image preprocessing techniques and feature extraction methods.

Our findings demonstrate that iris recognition using a database of iris images obtained in visible light using a smartphone camera is a viable and accurate method for biometric identification. This approach has the potential to be used in various applications, such as mobile device authentication, access control, and identity verification.

title: Jacobo Palm
text:

title: Nell Mangel

title: A Novel Domain Adaptation Framework for Medical Image Segmentation
text:
In this paper, we propose a novel domain adaptation framework for medical image segmentation, which addresses the challenging problem of segmenting images from unseen domains. Our approach leverages a combination of domain-invariant feature learning and adversarial training to effectively adapt a segmentation model to new domains. We evaluate our framework on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate its superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods.

Medical image segmentation is a critical task in healthcare, with applications in disease diagnosis, treatment planning, and monitoring. However, segmentation models are typically trained on datasets from a single domain, and their performance degrades significantly when applied to images from unseen domains. This domain shift problem arises from variations in image acquisition protocols, patient populations, and artifacts, among other factors.

To overcome this challenge, we propose a domain adaptation framework that learns domain-invariant features and adapts the segmentation model to new domains using adversarial training. Our approach consists of two main components: a feature alignment module and a domain classification module. The feature alignment module aligns the features of source and target domains, while the domain classification module classifies the images into their corresponding domains.

We evaluate our framework on several benchmark datasets, including brain tumor segmentation, lung nodule segmentation, and retinal vessel segmentation. Our results show that our framework outperforms state-of-the-art domain adaptation methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness to unseen domains. We also perform a series of ablation studies to analyze the effectiveness of the individual components of our framework.

Our main contributions are:

* A novel domain adaptation framework for medical image segmentation that combines domain-invariant feature learning and adversarial training.
* A feature alignment module that aligns the features of source and target domains, enabling the segmentation model to learn domain-invariant features.
* A domain classification module that classifies the images into their corresponding domains, enabling the segmentation model to adapt to new domains.
* Extensive evaluations on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating the superior performance and robustness of our framework compared to state-of-the-art methods.

title: Barney Frank
text:
Barney Frank (born March 31, 1940) is an American politician who served as a member of the U.S. House of Representatives from Massachusetts from 1981 to 2013. He was a leading co-sponsor of the Dodd–Frank Act, which implemented sweeping reforms of the financial industry in the wake of the financial crisis of 2007–2008.

A member of the Democratic Party, Frank served as chairman of the House Financial Services Committee from 2007 to 2011. He was a prominent figure in the late-2000s effort to pass housing reform legislation and played a central role in the debate over financial regulation after the financial crisis.

Frank was born in Bayonne, New Jersey, and raised in Newton, Massachusetts. He graduated from Harvard College in 1962 and then from Harvard Law School in 1965. He began his political career working for Congressman Michael Harrington. He was elected to the Massachusetts House of Representatives in 1972 and the Massachusetts Senate in 1974. He was elected to the U.S. House of Representatives in 1980 and has been reelected every term since.

In 1987, he came out as the first member of Congress to publicly acknowledge that he is gay. He has been married to James Ready since 2012.

Frank was a leading co-sponsor of the Dodd–Frank Act, which implemented sweeping reforms of the financial industry in the wake of the financial crisis of 2007–2008. The legislation created the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, which is tasked with protecting consumers from predatory lending practices, and established new regulations on the financial industry.

Frank has been a vocal critic of the Trump administration, and has accused the president of "deliberately sabotaging" the Affordable Care Act. He has also been critical of the administration's handling of the investigation into Russian interference in the 2016 election.

title: Color Image Segmentation using Adaptive Particle Swarm Optimization and Fuzzy C-means
text:
This paper proposes a novel approach to color image segmentation using adaptive particle swarm optimization (PSO) and fuzzy c-means (FCM) clustering. Traditional PSO algorithms have been limited by their inability to adapt to changing particle populations, leading to converged solutions that are not always optimal. In this work, an adaptive PSO algorithm is proposed that dynamically adjusts the population size based on the convergence progress of the optimization process. The adaptive PSO algorithm is combined with FCM clustering to separate the image into its constituent parts.

The proposed method was tested on several benchmark images and compared to existing methods, including traditional PSO and FCM. The results show that the adaptive PSO-FCM algorithm outperforms these methods in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. Moreover, the proposed method can handle images with varying illumination conditions and noise levels without requiring any preprocessing steps.

The main contribution of this paper lies in the development of an adaptive PSO algorithm that can effectively optimize the objective function in color image segmentation problems. By leveraging the advantages of both PSO and FCM, the proposed method provides a more robust and efficient solution to this challenging problem. Future research directions may include applying the proposed method to other optimization problems in computer vision and exploring ways to further improve its performance.

The project is being initiated by social journalist David Smith, who intends to use the project to explore the idea of young citizens being offered the opportunity to vote online.

"I don't think that by the time young women are 18 they automatically remain active or socially inactive," he responded. "There are a bunch of politicians with similar opinions on this but no-one is arguing that it shouldn't be done and so maybe this is a project which the coalition will put behind and one which the opposition parties will try to show that they are open to as well."

title: Attention U-Net: Learning Where to Look for the Pancreas
text:
In this paper, we present a novel approach for improving the accuracy of pancreas segmentation in medical images using a technique called Attention U-Net. The pancreas is a vital organ that plays an essential role in digestion and glucose regulation, and its accurate segmentation is crucial for diagnosis and treatment of various pancreatic diseases. However, manual segmentation of the pancreas can be time-consuming and challenging due to its complex shape and location near other organs.

To address this challenge, we propose an attention mechanism that learns to focus on the most relevant regions when segmenting the pancreas. Our proposed method uses a U-Net architecture with an additional attention branch that learns to predict a weight map indicating the importance of each pixel in the input image. This attention map is then used to guide the feature extraction process, allowing the network to selectively focus on pixels that are most informative for pancreas segmentation.

We evaluate our Attention U-Net on a dataset of contrast-enhanced CT scans and compare it to traditional U-Net architectures without attention. Our results show that Attention U-Net achieves significantly higher segmentation accuracy than existing methods (mean Dice score = 0.87 vs. 0.83), while also reducing computational cost by approximately 25%. We further analyze the attention maps generated by our model and find that they accurately identify key features such as the pancreatic duct and blood vessels, which are important for successful segmentation.

Our work demonstrates the potential of incorporating attention mechanisms into deep learning models for medical image segmentation tasks, particularly for organs with complex shapes and locations like the pancreas. By selectively focusing on relevant regions, Attention U-Net offers a promising solution for improving segmentation accuracy and efficiency in clinical settings.

title: Adaptive strategy for superpixel-based region-growing image segmentation
text:
This work presents a region-growing image segmentation approach based on
superpixel decomposition. From an initial contour-constrained over-segmentation
of the input image, the image segmentation is achieved by iteratively merging
similar superpixels into regions. This approach raises two key issues: (1) how
to compute the similarity between superpixels in order to perform accurate
merging and (2) in which order those superpixels must be merged together. In
this perspective, we firstly introduce a robust adaptive multi-scale superpixel
similarity in which region comparisons are made both at content and common
border level. Secondly, we propose a global merging strategy to efficiently
guide the region merging process. Such strategy uses an adpative merging
criterion to ensure that best region aggregations are given highest priorities.
This allows to reach a final segmentation into consistent regions with strong
boundary adherence. We perform experiments on the BSDS500 image dataset to
highlight to which extent our method compares favorably against other
well-known image segmentation algorithms. The obtained results demonstrate the
promising potential of the proposed approach.

title: Few-shot Medical Image Segmentation using a Global Correlation Network with Discriminative Embedding
text:
In this paper, we propose a novel approach for few-shot medical image segmentation using a Global Correlation Network with Discriminative Embedding (GCN-DE). Medical image segmentation is a critical task in healthcare, but it can be challenging due to the complexity and variability of medical images. Few-shot learning, which enables models to learn from a small number of labeled examples, has the potential to improve the efficiency and accuracy of medical image segmentation.

However, few-shot learning in medical image segmentation is particularly challenging due to the high dimensionality and variability of medical images. To address this challenge, we propose the GCN-DE model, which combines a Global Correlation Network (GCN) with a Discriminative Embedding (DE) module. The GCN captures long-range dependencies in medical images, while the DE module learns a compact and discriminative embedding space that can be used for few-shot segmentation.

The GCN-DE model is trained on a large dataset of medical images and achieves state-of-the-art performance on a variety of segmentation tasks, including brain tumor segmentation, liver segmentation, and lung segmentation. We also conduct a series of ablation studies to evaluate the effectiveness of the GCN and DE modules, and demonstrate that the combination of these two modules leads to improved performance compared to using either module alone.

Our main contributions are:

* The proposal of a novel few-shot medical image segmentation approach using a Global Correlation Network with Discriminative Embedding (GCN-DE).
* The development of a new network architecture that combines a Global Correlation Network (GCN) with a Discriminative Embedding (DE) module.
* The achievement of state-of-the-art performance on a variety of medical image segmentation tasks using the GCN-DE model.
* The demonstration of the effectiveness of the GCN and DE modules through ablation studies.

Overall, our work has the potential to improve the efficiency and accuracy of medical image segmentation, and could potentially be applied to a wide range of medical image analysis tasks.

title: Jay Schlueter

He has been involved in the technology business for over three generations and has earned recognition for his experience in brand innovation, strategy, and marketing. Early Life and Career

Schlueter was born on September 21, 1975, in San Diego, CA. He grew up in a household of technology professionals and had a strong interest in computer technology from an early age. After finishing high school, he attended Stanford University, where he earned a Master's degree in Engineering Engineering. Career

title: Geography of Missouri
text:
Texas, a county near the geographic centre of the United States, has two different geological divisions:  a north-western coastal plain or prairie region portion of the Interior Plains' Eastern Lowland (areas Osage Plain 12f and Dissected Till Plains 12e) known as the coastal plains
 a grassland in the extreme southwest bootheel area of Mississippi, portion of the Gulf Plain known as the Missouri Alluvial Plain (areas 3e) or the Missouri embayment
 the Missouri part of the Mississippi Mountains (regions 14a and 14b) which lies between the Missouri Alluvial Plain and the Southern lowland.
The boundary between the central plains and the Mississippi region follows the 
Mississippi River from its mouth at St. Joseph to Washington. This also corresponds to the southernmost extent of glaciation during the Pre-Illinoian Stage which destroyed the remnant plateau to the southeast but left the ancient landforms to the east intact. The Kansas boundary runs northwest from there towards Missouri at the northeastern corner of Missouri. The boundary between the Ozark and lowland states goes west from Cape Girardeau on the Missouri River to the Texas border just northwest of Pine Grove. Arkansas borders nine other US States, more than any other nation besides Texas, which only borders three counties.

title: Drospirenone/ethinylestradiol/levomefolic acid
text:
Drospirenone/ethinylestradiol/levomefolic acid (INN, USAN, trade name Natazia) is a combined oral contraceptive pill manufactured by Bayer Schering Pharma. It was approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on May 28, 2010, and is indicated for the prevention of pregnancy in women who elect to use an oral contraceptive.

The active ingredients in Natazia are:

Drospirenone: a synthetic progestin with antiandrogenic and antimineralocorticoid properties

Ethinylestradiol: a synthetic estrogen

Levomefolic acid: a natural folate

The combination of these three active ingredients is unique to Natazia and is not found in any other oral contraceptive pill on the market.

The most common side effects associated with Natazia are:

Headache

Nausea

Breast tenderness

Irregular bleeding

These side effects are generally mild and resolve with continued use of the medication.

Serious side effects associated with Natazia are rare, but can include:

Blood clots

Stroke

Heart attack

If you experience any of these serious side effects, stop taking Natazia and seek medical attention immediately.

If you are considering taking Natazia, or any other oral contraceptive pill, be sure to talk to your healthcare provider first. He or she can help you determine if this medication is right for you and can answer any questions you may have.

title: Large-scale image segmentation based on distributed clustering algorithms
text:
This paper presents a scalable approach to large-scale image segmentation through the utilization of distributed clustering algorithms. With the growing availability of high-dimensional data, traditional centralized processing methods have become increasingly inefficient and limited by computational constraints. To address this challenge, we propose a novel framework that enables the parallelization of image segmentation across multiple nodes in a distributed computing environment.

Our proposed method leverages the power of distributed clustering algorithms, which are proven to be highly effective in handling massive datasets, to perform pixel-level classification and segmentation of images. By partitioning the input image into smaller chunks and distributing them across multiple processors, our approach achieves unprecedented levels of scalability and efficiency. We demonstrate the efficacy of our technique by applying it to several large-scale image datasets, yielding superior performance and accuracy compared to state-of-the-art centralized methods.

The key contributions of this paper can be summarized as follows:

1. A distributed clustering-based framework for large-scale image segmentation is introduced, which enabled the efficient processing of massive images via parallel computation.
2. An optimization strategy was developed to effectively distribute the workload and minimize communication overheads between processor nodes.
3. Thorough experiments were conducted on various large-scale image datasets to evaluate the performance of the proposed method against existing centralized approaches. The results show significant improvements in both efficiency and accuracy.
4. The proposed method paves the way for tackling even larger imaging datasets, previously considered too vast for practical analysis, opening up new opportunities in applications such as computer vision, machine learning, and multimedia processing.

In conclusion, this paper offers a groundbreaking solution to the problem of large-scale image segmentation, providing an elegant combination of distributed computing and clustering algorithms that facilitates efficient and accurate processing of huge amounts of image data. Our approach has far-reaching implications for advancing research and developing innovative applications within the realm of big data analytics.

title: Honoré Desmond Sharrer
text: Honoré Desmond Sharrer (February 12, 1920 – January 17, 2009) was an American painter. She first earned public praise in 1950 for her painting Tribute to the American Working People, a five-image polyptych designed in the form of a Baroque altarpiece, except that its central figure is a factory worker and not a patron. Flanking this central figure are smaller scenes of everyday people—at a picnic, in a parlor, on a farm and in the schoolroom. Meticulously painted in oil on composition board in a style and colour palette reminiscent of the Flemish Masters, the finished work is more than five inches long and six inches high and took her three months to complete. It was the subject of a 2007 exhibition at the Smithsonian Institute and is part of the permanent collection of the Smithsonian Asian Art Institute. She first earned public notice when her work Workers and Artists (1943) was included in the legendary 1946 "Fourteen Americans" show at the Museum of Contemporary Art in New York, curated by William Canning Smith. This show included a selection of up and coming painters including Alexander Motherwell, Akira Noguchi (sculptor), and David Goodman. The "Four Americans" show at the Museum of Contemporary Art, while widely thought to proclaim the arrival of abstract expressionism did not do so unambiguously because it included those like Sharrer and John Tooker who are not modernists based on the litmus test of abstraction.

title: Dense 3D Visual Mapping via Semantic Simplification
text:
In this paper, we present a novel approach to dense 3D visual mapping that leverages semantic simplification to efficiently represent complex environments. Existing methods often struggle with the trade-off between detail and efficiency, either providing highly detailed but computationally expensive maps or simplified but incomplete representations. Our proposed method addresses this challenge by introducing asemantic simplification step that extracts the most important features of the environment while reducing the computational cost.

We evaluate our approach on several publicly available datasets and demonstrate its superior performance in terms of both accuracy and efficiency compared to state-of-the-art methods. Specifically, our method achieves higher point cloud segmentation accuracy and more efficient map construction, while also providing a more compact representation of the environment. Additionally, we showcase the versatility of our approach by applying it to various applications such as object recognition, scene understanding, and autonomous navigation.

Our main contributions can be summarized as follows:

* A novel approach to dense 3D visual mapping that combines semantic simplification with efficient map construction
* APointNet-like network architecture that integrates semantic information into the mapping process
* An effective simplification strategy that reduces the computational cost while preserving essential details of the environment
* State-of-the-art performance in both accuracy and efficiency on several benchmark datasets
* Demonstration of the versatility of our approach through various applications

The rest of the paper is organized as follows: related work is reviewed in Section 2, followed by the methodology description in Section 3. Results and evaluations are presented in Section 4, while Section 5 concludes the paper and outlines future work directions.

title: A Generalized Asymmetric Dual-front Model for Active Contours and Image Segmentation
text:
The Voronoi diagram-based dual-front active contour models are known as a
powerful and efficient way for addressing the image segmentation and domain
partitioning problems. In the basic formulation of the dual-front models, the
evolving contours can be considered as the interfaces of adjacent Voronoi
regions. Among these dual-front models, a crucial ingredient is regarded as the
geodesic metrics by which the geodesic distances and the corresponding Voronoi
diagram can be estimated. In this paper, we introduce a type of asymmetric
quadratic metrics dual-front model. The metrics considered are built by the
integration of the image features and a vector field derived from the evolving
contours. The use of the asymmetry enhancement can reduce the risk of contour
shortcut or leakage problems especially when the initial contours are far away
from the target boundaries or the images have complicated intensity
distributions. Moreover, the proposed dual-front model can be applied for image
segmentation in conjunction with various region-based homogeneity terms. The
numerical experiments on both synthetic and real images show that the proposed
dual-front model indeed achieves encouraging results.

title: Computing Valid p-values for Image Segmentation by Selective Inference
text:
The paper "Computing Valid p-values for Image Segmentation by Selective Inference" presents a novel approach to computing valid p-values for image segmentation techniques. Traditional methods of evaluating segmentation algorithms rely on arbitrarily defined thresholds or subjective visual inspection, which can lead to inconsistent and unreliable results.

In this work, we propose a method based on selective inference that allows for the computation of valid p-values for image segmentation. Our approach leverages recent advances in statistical inference and machine learning to provide a principled way of evaluating the significance of segmentation results. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method through experiments on several benchmark datasets, where we show that it provides more accurate and robust assessments of segmentation performance compared to traditional methods.

The key contribution of this paper is the introduction of a new evaluation framework for image segmentation that is grounded in statistical hypothesis testing. By treating segmentation as a hypothesis test, we can compute p-values that indicate the probability that the observed segmentation result occurred by chance. This allows us to quantify the uncertainty in segmentation results and provides a meaningful way to compare the performance of different algorithms.

Our proposed method has important implications for the field of image segmentation, as it enables researchers to evaluate and compare segmentation algorithms in a more objective and reliable manner. It also opens up new avenues for future research, such as investigating the relationship between segmentation performance and underlying factors like image quality or object size. Overall, this work represents an important step towards developing a more rigorous understanding of image segmentation and its limitations.

The people of the town rally round him, and victory is theirs. The novel ends on a note of victory and celebration, and pays tribute to the gallantry of Jack and the common people who never once shrank from defending their rights and their home. title: Training dog not to go over threshold on walks. How much longer?

I’m wondering from people who’ve experienced something similar how long it took for your dog to have calmer walks and when you stopped needing to treat all the time or if you stopped at all. title: AITA For not wanting to help an ex friend's kid?
text:
Absolutely not! I don't think you're a terrible person for not wanting to help out your ex-friend's kid. It's understandable that you might not want to be involved with your ex's life anymore, especially if the friendship ended on bad terms.

It's important to remember that you're not obligated to help anyone, let alone someone who was never actually a close friend of yours. If you don't feel like helping out, it's okay to politely decline or even ignore the request altogether. You have every right to prioritize your own time and resources however you see fit.

That being said, if you do decide you want to help, there are ways to do so without compromising your own wellbeing or finances. You could try offering advice or guidance, providing emotional support, or connecting them with other people who might be better equipped to assist their needs. Ultimately, how much—or how little—you choose to help is completely up to you. Just make sure your decision aligns with what feels most comfortable for YOU.

title: YouTube-VOS: A Large-Scale Video Object Segmentation Benchmark
text:
In this paper, we present YouTube-VOS, a large-scale video object segmentation benchmark that provides a comprehensive evaluation framework for video object segmentation (VOS) algorithms. VOS is an important task in computer vision that involves separating objects of interest from their background and other objects in a video sequence. Despite its significance, there is a lack of large-scale benchmarks for VOS, which hinders the development and evaluation of VOS algorithms.

YouTube-VOS addresses this issue by providing a dataset of 4,417 video clips, totaling 150,000 frames, with annotated objects across various categories, including animals, vehicles, and humans. The dataset is diverse, covering various scenarios such as object movement, occlusion, and cluttered backgrounds. We also introduce a new evaluation metric, called Video Object Segmentation Quality (VOSQ), which combines both temporal and spatial metrics to provide a comprehensive measure of VOS performance.

We evaluate several state-of-the-art VOS algorithms on YouTube-VOS and analyze their performance. Our results show that existing VOS algorithms struggle with objects that undergo significant motion or deformation, and that there is a need for better algorithms that can handle these challenges. We also demonstrate the utility of YouTube-VOS in evaluating the performance of VOS algorithms under different scenarios and provide insights into the strengths and weaknesses of various approaches.

YouTube-VOS is a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners working on VOS, and we believe it will play an important role in advancing the field of video object segmentation. Our hope is that YouTube-VOS will encourage the development of more sophisticated VOS algorithms that can handle the challenges of real-world videos and contribute to various applications such as video surveillance, autonomous driving, and video editing.

title: Combinatorial Energy Learning for Image Segmentation
text:
We introduce a new machine learning approach for image segmentation that uses
a neural network to model the conditional energy of a segmentation given an
image. Our approach, combinatorial energy learning for image segmentation
(CELIS) places a particular emphasis on modeling the inherent combinatorial
nature of dense image segmentation problems. We propose efficient algorithms
for learning deep neural networks to model the energy function, and for local
optimization of this energy in the space of supervoxel agglomerations. We
extensively evaluate our method on a publicly available 3-D microscopy dataset
with 25 billion voxels of ground truth data. On an 11 billion voxel test set,
we find that our method improves volumetric reconstruction accuracy by more
than 20% as compared to two state-of-the-art baseline methods: graph-based
segmentation of the output of a 3-D convolutional neural network trained to
predict boundaries, as well as a random forest classifier trained to
agglomerate supervoxels that were generated by a 3-D convolutional neural
network.

title: Leucodecton canescens
text:
Leucodecton canescens is a species of snake in the Colubridae family.

It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests, subtropical or tropical swamps, and intermittent freshwater marshes.


This species grows to a total length (including tail) of around 1.5 m (5 ft). It is a slender snake with a long, narrow head. The colouration is variable, but it is usually some shade of brown, with darker cross-bands.

title: A Summons to Memphis
text: "A Summons to Memphis" is an eventful and heart-rending narrative of the life of Philip Carver, a middle-aged editor living a quiet and modest life in New York City. The story takes a turn when he is called back home by his two elderly sisters, because of the strange behavior of their father. Once there, he returns to the past and to the family history. A dominant figure in the past and in the present is the authoritarian father, who ruthlessly uprooted the family from the quiet life of Nashville and moved to Memphis, in order to remake his life after a business failure. The siblings were under the father's rigorous regimen and his inscrutable presence, unable to form relationships and live independently. Through the reminiscences of Philip, the book reveals the fragile balance of family life, the difficult relationships between siblings, and the restraining influence of the past. The past becomes present as Philip, his sisters and their manipulative father come to terms with their shared past. As the story develops, the strange behavior of the father gradually reveals itself to be a new attempt to marry, which the adult children take as a bad sign for the family's uneasy relationship. In the face of the family's mistrustful past, the members of the family conspire against the father, and this leads to a series of unexpected and revelatory events. "A Summons to Memphis" is a powerful narrative of the complexities of the family, the restraining power of the past, the struggle for individuality under the control of the parents, and the myriad ways in which memories comfort, break and change the present.

title: Albert Angelo
text: In B. S. J. Onomasty’s Albert Angelo, the character – Albert Angelo – is an architect who dreams of building buildings that will endure through the ages. But Albert Angelo is an extremely pious man, and in spite of his talents and his love for his work, he finds himself unable to find success in his chosen profession. He spends his days working on projects that are unfulfilling, working with difficult clients, and he himself remains unable to realize his own personal creative goals. Parallel to his struggles in his professional life, he is struggling with his own personal life, haunted by a failed love affair and a failed marriage. As he begins to delve into the complexities of his personal relationships, Albert Angelo is forced to face his own shortcomings and how they have affected the people around him. As Albert Angelo’s professional and personal lives converge, the novel explores themes of self-realization, ambition, and the search for meaning. The author’s narrative is beautifully crafted, and his storyline presents a moving portrait of a man who, despite setbacks, never gives up on his dreams. A novel of many layers, Albert Angelo’s style is unique and experimental. Using footnotes, diagrams, and typographical experiments, the book is a multi-layered, complex novel that breaks the bounds of a straightforward narrative. In the end, Albert Angelo is a heartbreaking look at one man’s struggle to find meaning and fulfillment in a world that is often cold and indifferent. It is a book that questions the meaning of life and the meaning of love, and a book that questions how we create, love, and live.

title: A Universal Parallel Two-Pass MDL Context Tree Compression Algorithm
text:
Computing problems that handle large amounts of data necessitate the use of
lossless data compression for efficient storage and transmission. We present a
novel lossless universal data compression algorithm that uses parallel
computational units to increase the throughput. The length-$N$ input sequence
is partitioned into $B$ blocks. Processing each block independently of the
other blocks can accelerate the computation by a factor of $B$, but degrades
the compression quality. Instead, our approach is to first estimate the minimum
description length (MDL) context tree source underlying the entire input, and
then encode each of the $B$ blocks in parallel based on the MDL source. With
this two-pass approach, the compression loss incurred by using more parallel
units is insignificant. Our algorithm is work-efficient, i.e., its
computational complexity is $O(N/B)$. Its redundancy is approximately
$B\log(N/B)$ bits above Rissanen's lower bound on universal compression
performance, with respect to any context tree source whose maximal depth is at
most $\log(N/B)$. We improve the compression by using different quantizers for
states of the context tree based on the number of symbols corresponding to
those states. Numerical results from a prototype implementation suggest that
our algorithm offers a better trade-off between compression and throughput than
competing universal data compression algorithms.

title:
Photoelectric effect induced by blackbody radiation: a theoretical
  analysis of a potential heat energy harvesting mechanism
text:
The photoelectric effect induced by blackbody radiation could be a mechanism
to harvest ambient thermal energy at a uniform temperature. Here, I describe
(without going too much into mathematical details) the theoretical model I
developed starting from 2010 to study that phenomenon, and I summarize the
results of the numerical simulations. Simulations tell us that the process must
be there. Moreover, at least two experimental tests have been performed in the
past years that seem to corroborate, although not definitely, the alleged
functioning of the proposed mechanism. Unfortunately, at present, the
obtainable power density is extremely low and inadequate for immediate
practical applications.

title: Mixing and double recurrence in probability groups
text:
We define a class of groups equipped with an invariant probability measure,
which includes all compact groups and is closed under taking ultraproducts with
the induced Loeb measure; in fact, this class also contains the ultraproducts
all locally compact unimodular amenable groups. We call the members of this
class probability groups and develop the basics of the theory of their
measure-preserving actions on probability spaces, including a natural notion of
mixing. A short proof reveals that for probability groups mixing implies double
recurrence, which generalizes a theorem of Bergelson and Tao proved for
ultraproducts of finite groups. Moreover, a quantitative version of our proof
gives that $\varepsilon$-approximate mixing implies
$3\sqrt{\varepsilon}$-approximate double recurrence. Examples of approximately
mixing probability groups are quasirandom groups introduced by Gowers, so the
last theorem generalizes and sharpens the corresponding results for quasirandom
groups of Bergelson and Tao, as well as of Austin. Lastly, we point out that
the fact that the ultraproduct of locally compact unimodular amenable groups is
a probability group provides a general alternative to Furstenberg
correspondence principle.

title: What hatches out of the egg?
text:
This is what hatched out of an egg in my backyard! I had no idea what kind of bird laid this strange, speckled egg in our garden, but now I know for sure.

At first, it was tiny and wobbly. Its stubby wings were useless, and its legs seemed to be made of jelly. It couldn't stand up or walk properly, it could only waddle around on spindly little feet that kept collapsing beneath it. Even though it was sohelpless, something about those big round eyes gave me the courage to hope. I fed it some water from an eyedropper because it clearly needed help. The next day, there was poop everywhere! That messy baby had somehow managed to craphandle itself, get its feathers dirty, and generally make a huge pother. Since then, it won'the even let me near it without hissing angrily at me and trying to peck my fingers with its pointed beak! Featherare growing fast all over its bald, wrinkled head--I read online they take about two weeks to grow fully-functional adult plumage after they hatch. In the meantime, I can tell whether it wants food,water,or attention by which part of its very expressive face is puffedup & openedwide (either the beak, the mouth, or the anus). What do you think --chicken?duckling?frog?Noneoftherestseemmaternaldovian, turtles don't havebeaks...guesseswelcome!

title: I know it's toxic but I would be happier skinnier

title: Cadmus of Miletus
text:
Cadmus of Miletus (Greek: Κάδμος ὁ Μιλήσιος; fl. c. 6th century BC) was a Greek architect, engineer and sculptor from Miletus in Ionia. He is credited with being the first architect to use the Corinthian order.

Cadmus is first mentioned in the works of the Greek historian Herodotus, who says that he was the son of the king of Phoenicia. According to Herodotus, Cadmus was sent by his father to Greece to find a suitable site for a new Phoenician colony. He arrived in Greece and settled on the island of Thera, where he built a city which he named after himself, Cadmeia.

Herodotus goes on to say that Cadmus then set out in search of his sister Europa, who had been abducted by Zeus. He eventually found her in Boeotia, where she was being held captive by the king of Thebes. Cadmus fought and killed the king, and freed Europa.

Afterwards, Zeus turned the king of Thebes into a dragon, and Cadmus killed the dragon with the help of Athena. Athena then told Cadmus to sow the dragon's teeth in the ground, from which a race of warriors, the Spartoi, would spring.

Cadmus did as he was instructed, and the Spartoi did indeed spring from the ground, fully armed and ready for battle. However, they immediately turned on Cadmus and began fighting amongst themselves. The only survivors were five men who agreed to spare Cadmus's life on the condition that he abandon his quest for Europa and instead marry Harmonia, the daughter of Ares and Aphrodite.

Cadmus and Harmonia had four sons: Polydorus, Illyrius, Cadmus and Autolycus. Cadmus eventually left Thebes and founded the city of Corinth, where he ruled as king for many years. He was eventually turned into a snake by Hera, and was later worshipped as a god of wisdom by the people of Corinth.

title: Girls on Boys
text:
"Girls on Boys" is a song by Norwegian electronic dance song producer trio Galantis and British singer-songwriter Rozes. It was written by Rozes, Peter Jonback, Rasmus Cantoreggi, Svidden, Khalid Salmani, Galantis, Michael Gad and Robert Cumbee, with production handled by the latter two and Afsheen. The song was released through Atlantic Records and BMG International on 1 March 2017, as the first promotional single from the trio's third studio album, The Aviary (2017). Background
Galantis spoke of the album in a press release: "It's a style of writing that's been a part of Galantis from the start, but we never quite had the opportunity to show you. We had our battles with this thing. It lasted a thousand turns, but it only forced us to be anywhere we haven't been before, and we're stoked to be sharing." Rozes described the motivation behind the album, stating:"'Girls On Boys' is about trying to resolve a broken heart with a night of flashy distractions, which is only a short-term solution. Two of my co-writers came through a break-up and we were arguing about how he was coping, which was basically by staying busy, hanging out with strangers, and partying like nothing was okay."She furthered: "The upbeat vibe of the album masks the darker songs, which reveal that the money, diamonds and champagne won't fix the sense of missing the man you love and feeling alone." Galantis subsequently announced the dates for The Aviary concert in Autumn in celebration of the single release.

title: Moskvitch 2140
text: Moskvitch 2140 series is large family automobile produced by Russian automotive manufacturer AZLK from October 1976 to 1988. It came first as Moskvitch 2138 and Moskvitch 2140 on a modified 412 platform. Pre-production prototypes were shown during 1975. Beginning in 1981, the modernised modification of the M-2140 export/luxury model was initially marketed and branded "2140 SP" in the Eastern Bloc regions and "1500 SP" outside. The most significant differences between the three models were redesigned dashboard and rear passenger headrests in the M-2140. Beginning in 1982, the M-2138 models were discontinued and the M-2140 was the only Moskvitch cars available in all markets. It was face-lifted the same day: the shield insignia was altered to feature "АЗЛК" (AZLK) written in blue outline, the hood coating changed from aluminum to metal, and both side mirrors were significantly revised to be more heavy. The station wagon variant M-2137 was the first of Soviet vehicles to not feature taillight fins to accommodate door opening, until the model was discontinued in 1985.

title: Not getting the love we deserved
text: I realised today that we never actually got the love we deserved from our parents. I used to convince myself that “they weren’t that bad” and the love bombing stages made me think it was just “normal fighting” but it’s not. I grew up bullied as well and so neither school or home was my safe space which was the reason I read so much and threw myself into fictional worlds. Maladaptive daydreaming was my escape. It’s only recently that I have a healthy bunch of friends that I can say they’re my safe space especially since I still live with my parents but it’s a punch in the gut to think the people who are supposed to give you that unconditional healthy love that you can rely on and always come home to gave us the kind of love we have to spend the rest of our lives trying to unlearn and escape From. It’s incredibly damaging because then we tend to seek that healthy love in our romantic relationships and friendships to make up for what we never got as kids. We’re not supposed to seek it out like that it was supposed to been given to us by our parents but they never did. It’s hard to admit being unloved but that’s what it is.

title: Google to scan famous libraries
text:
Google will scan famous libraries and make them accessible online for free, under an agreement with the British Museum. The search giant has agreed to scan more than 1,000 manuscripts in the National Library of Wales (NLS) and the Bodleian Library at Edinburgh Campus. Google's scanning service will be released on Friday, but it will only cover the NLS and Bodleian collections. It will not include the Royal Collection at Westminster or the British Library. The deal was struck after a year-long evaluation process involving library staff, administrators and students. The move comes as part of Facebook's wider move into electronic products such as its Android phone operating system and its Chrome browser. The firm stated that it will only offer access to the digitised content through its own site.

I'm afraid this is just the instance of how Facebook is going to get citizens to use their services. They are actually doing this by providing free Wi-Fi in public areas, so why not do the same way for movies? I think they don't have to pay royalties to the writers who wrote those novels.

title: Daughter of Darkness
text: The novel is about a young woman, Seraphina, born into a family of witches. The inhabitants of the little village where she lives live in fear of her, believing them to be bewitched. Seraphina, however, is different from the others. She has a rare gift—the power of controlling darkness. Her parents and the people of the village fear her, and a longing for acceptance grows up within her. Her friendship with the young man Thomas, who is not afraid of her, is a comfort to her. The two are fated to fall in love, which complicates Seraphina’s life. Then, when a powerful and malicious witch from a rival family learns of Seraphina’s extraordinary gifts, she sees an opportunity for her to seize power over the whole of the village and surrounding district. She entices Thomas into her service, and Seraphina has to face up to her own fear and to overcome her own darkness in order to save him. Daughter of Darkness is a thrilling novel that keeps you on the edge of your seat right up to the last line.

title: CAKES: Channel-wise Automatic KErnel Shrinking for Efficient 3D Networks
text:
3D Convolution Neural Networks (CNNs) have been widely applied to 3D scene
understanding, such as video analysis and volumetric image recognition.
However, 3D networks can easily lead to over-parameterization which incurs
expensive computation cost. In this paper, we propose Channel-wise Automatic
KErnel Shrinking (CAKES), to enable efficient 3D learning by shrinking standard
3D convolutions into a set of economic operations e.g., 1D, 2D convolutions.
Unlike previous methods, CAKES performs channel-wise kernel shrinkage, which
enjoys the following benefits: 1) enabling operations deployed in every layer
to be heterogeneous, so that they can extract diverse and complementary
information to benefit the learning process; and 2) allowing for an efficient
and flexible replacement design, which can be generalized to both
spatial-temporal and volumetric data. Further, we propose a new search space
based on CAKES, so that the replacement configuration can be determined
automatically for simplifying 3D networks. CAKES shows superior performance to
other methods with similar model size, and it also achieves comparable
performance to state-of-the-art with much fewer parameters and computational
costs on tasks including 3D medical imaging segmentation and video action
recognition. Codes and models are available at
https://github.com/yucornetto/CAKES

title: Werewolf versus Dragon
text: In this weepy tale of Werewolf vs. Dragon, the peaceful village of Eldridge is shattered to atoms when a savage dragon swoops down from the mountains to terrorize the villagers. The hero of the piece, a young blacksmith called Ethan, is a werewolf, and is not averse to keeping the secret to himself for fear of his town’s superstitions. At first he is reluctant to reveal his true nature to the villagers for fear of their reaction. But then the dragon’s attacks become more frequent and more deadly, and he realizes that he is the only one who can save Eldridge. He sets out on a quest to master his werewolf powers, and seeks advice from the wise and mysterious hermit, Morwen, who lives deep in the forest. Meanwhile, the dragon, Ignis, is not the mindless monster the villagers think he is. He is an ancient being, a creature of extraordinary powers who was banished from his home by a cruel dragon-hunter. He sought refuge in the mountains near Eldridge, where he was overcome by fear and anger, and became a danger to the people in the village. As Ethan continues to develop his werewolf powers, he slowly begins to discover the truth behind Ignis’s identity. He realizes that they are both misunderstood creatures, hunted and feared by humans. This makes him resolve to find a peaceful solution. But then the dragon-hunter who banished Ignis arrives in Eldridge, and the conflict escalates beyond his control. Ethan now has to battle not only the dragon, but the dragon-hunter and the villagers’ fear. In an epic battle, Ethan uses the power of the werewolf and his new understanding of Ignis to save his village. Werewolf vs. Dragon is a story of courage, courage, and cooperation. It also contains the themes of fear, misunderstanding, and the destructive nature of prejudice, woven into a thrilling tale of fantasy adventure.

title: Demographics of Niger
text:
Niger is a developing country located in West Africa. It is bordered by Nigeria to the south, Benin to the southwest, Burkina Faso to the northwest, Mali to the north, and Algeria to the northeast. Niger covers a land area of 1.267 million square kilometres, making it the largest country in West Africa. The country's Sahara Desert region in the north is one of the hottest places in the world.

The majority of Nigeriens are Sunni Muslims. The urban population is mostly concentrated in the capital city of Niamey, while the rural population is mostly concentrated in the southern and eastern regions of the country. The official language of Niger is French, but various indigenous languages are also spoken, such as Hausa, Zarma, and Fulani.

As of 2016, the population of Niger was estimated to be 20,429,937. The population is growing at a rate of 3.03% per year. The median age of the population is 16.6 years, and the life expectancy is 60.3 years.

Niger is a predominantly agricultural country, with approximately 80% of the population engaged in subsistence farming. The main crops grown in Niger are millet, sorghum, cowpeas, and peanuts. The country is also a major producer of livestock, with cattle, sheep, and goats being the most common. The industry and services sectors of the economy are relatively underdeveloped, accounting for only 14% of GDP. Major industries in Niger include uranium mining, cement production, and the processing of agricultural products.

The majority of the population lives in rural areas, with only 22% of the population living in urban areas. The capital city of Niamey is the largest city in Niger, with a population of 1,975,551. Other major cities include Zinder, Maradi, Tahoua, and Agadez.

title: MPs demand 'Budget leak' answers
text:
A government commission says it needs "immediate explanation" from the Parliament over how the Budget was circulated online.

In a statement the Parliamentary Private Accounts Commission voiced "significant doubts about how the leak happened and who was responsible".

It has spoken to President John Abbott to ask for guidance on the safety of "the public's sensitive tax records".

The Government, meanwhile, says it has been informed by the Federal Accounting Office that the tax records were not at risk.

On Monday, the online publication of two leaked state budget papers was branded a "grave error" by the Treasury and was being questioned by Whitehall authorities.

The budget documents included lists of proposed taxation exemptions for businesses.

Council chair John Taylor, MP for Gainsborough, stated: "MPs will have to come to the bottom of what was wrong and will have questions at tomorrow's council session with the National Audit Office and HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC).

title: Pneumothorax Segmentation: Deep Learning Image Segmentation to predict Pneumothorax
text:
Computer vision has shown promising results in medical image processing.
Pneumothorax is a deadly condition and if not diagnosed and treated at time
then it causes death. It can be diagnosed with chest X-ray images. We need an
expert and experienced radiologist to predict whether a person is suffering
from pneumothorax or not by looking at the chest X-ray images. Everyone does
not have access to such a facility. Moreover, in some cases, we need quick
diagnoses. So we propose an image segmentation model to predict and give the
output a mask that will assist the doctor in taking this crucial decision. Deep
Learning has proved their worth in many areas and outperformed man
state-of-the-art models. We want to use the power of these deep learning model
to solve this problem. We have used U-net [13] architecture with ResNet [17] as
a backbone and achieved promising results. U-net [13] performs very well in
medical image processing and semantic segmentation. Our problem falls in the
semantic segmentation category.

title: Deundra Hundon
text:
Deundra Hundon (born October 10, 1984) is an American basketball player who plays for the WNBA's Atlanta Dream.

Hundon was born in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. She played college basketball at Louisiana State University from 2002 to 2006. As a senior, she averaged 11.4 points, 2.8 rebounds and 2.9 assists per game.

After going undrafted in the 2006 WNBA Draft, Hundon signed with the New York Liberty. She played in 27 games for the Liberty, averaging 1.7 points per game.

In 2007, Hundon signed with the Atlanta Dream. She became a regular starter for the Dream in 2009, and helped the team to the WNBA Finals that year. Hundon has continued to be a starter for the Dream over the past few seasons.

title: Incorporating Near-Infrared Information into Semantic Image Segmentation
text:
This paper proposes a novel approach for incorporating near-infrared (NIR) information into semantic image segmentation. Semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that aims to assign a semantic label to each pixel in an image, such as road, building, or vegetation. Most existing semantic segmentation methods rely solely on visible light images, which can be limited in certain scenarios, such as low-light conditions or when the image is captured through a hazy atmosphere. In contrast, NIR images can provide valuable information about the scene, even in these challenging conditions.

The proposed approach leverages a deep learning framework to fuse visible and NIR images and improve the accuracy of semantic segmentation. The authors introduce a novel convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture that jointly processes the visible and NIR images, exploiting the complementary information between the two modalities. The network is trained on a large dataset of paired visible and NIR images, and the authors evaluate its performance on several benchmarks.

The results show that the proposed approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods that rely solely on visible light images, especially in low-light conditions. The authors also demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach in applications such as nighttime road detection and vegetation mapping.

The main contributions of this paper can be summarized as follows:

* The authors propose a novel deep learning approach for incorporating NIR information into semantic image segmentation.
* They introduce a CNN architecture that jointly processes visible and NIR images, leveraging the complementary information between the two modalities.
* The proposed approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods that rely solely on visible light images, especially in low-light conditions.
* The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach in various applications, such as nighttime road detection and vegetation mapping.

Overall, this paper provides a significant contribution to the field of semantic image segmentation, and its findings have important implications for a wide range of applications, including autonomous driving, environmental monitoring, and agricultural management.

title: A Distance Map Regularized CNN for Cardiac Cine MR Image Segmentation
text:
In this paper, we propose a novel deep learning approach for cardiac cine magnetic resonance (MR) image segmentation, which is a crucial step in various clinical applications such as heart disease diagnosis and treatment planning. Our method leverages the concept of distance map regularization to improve the accuracy and efficiency of the convolutional neural network (CNN).

Cardiac cine MR images are inherently high-dimensional and complex, making it challenging to accurately segment the left ventricle (LV) from the surrounding structures. Existing methods often rely on manually defined fixed-size filters or sliding window approaches, which may not effectively capture the spatial variations in cardiac morphology. Moreover, they can be computationally expensive and require extensive parameter tuning.

Our proposed method adopts a distance map regularization term that incorporates knowledge about the spatial relationships between neighboring pixels in the image. This term encourages the CNN to learn a smooth and continuous representation of the LV boundary, leading to improved segmentation performance. Furthermore, we introduce an efficient optimization scheme that enables real-time training of our model without sacrificing accuracy.

We evaluate our method on a large dataset of cardiac cine MR images and compare it with state-of-the-art algorithms. The results demonstrate that our approach achieves superior segmentation accuracy, while also providing faster processing times. Additionally, we perform thorough ablation studies to analyze the effectiveness of the distance map regularization term and provide insights into its contribution to the overall performance.

In conclusion, this paper presents a distance map regularized CNN for cardiac cine MR image segmentation, which offers improved accuracy and efficiency over existing methods. Our approach has important implications for clinical settings where timely and accurate LV segmentation is critical. Future work includes further exploring the potential of distance map regularization for other medical image segmentation tasks.

title: Iggie's House
text: The story, written by Judy Blume, is one of the most heartwarming of all. The story follows Winnie, a little girl who moves into a new house and befriends the Garber children, but soon realizes that the Garber children are not as friendly as she hoped. They are not interested in her and don't want to spend time with her. So, confused and hurt, she turns to her other neighbor, Iggie, an elderly lady who lives alone. Iggie is very helpful and gives Winnie valuable advice on how to behave with other people and how to make new friends. As the story unfolds, Winnie discovers that the Garber children's lack of interest in her has to do with her race. They are white, and they feel uncomfortable with her African-American origin and don't want to have anything to do with her. Winnie is shocked and hurt, but takes action and solves the problem herself. With Iggie's help, she organizes a neighborhood picnic to bring the community together and to raise awareness of the prejudices that exist. And the neighborhood picnic becomes a turning point and shows the importance of uniting as a group. Iggie's House is a touching story about prejudice, friendship and the importance of being kind.

title: Mumford-Shah Loss Functional for Image Segmentation with Deep Learning
text:
This paper proposes a novel approach to image segmentation using deep learning, specifically the Mumford-Shah loss functional. The Mumford-Shah loss functional is a regularization term that encourages the segmentation mask to have a piecewise constant structure, which is well-suited for images with complex structures. In this paper, we incorporate the Mumford-Shah loss functional into a deep learning framework for image segmentation, and demonstrate its effectiveness in segmenting images with varying levels of complexity.

Experiments conducted on several benchmark datasets show that the proposed method outperforms traditional deep learning-based segmentation methods, such as fully convolutional networks (FCNs) and U-Net, in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. We also show that the Mumford-Shah loss functional is able to capture the underlying structure of the images, leading to more accurate and interpretable segmentation results.

The main contributions of this paper are:

* The introduction of the Mumford-Shah loss functional for image segmentation with deep learning
* The development of an efficient optimization algorithm for minimizing the Mumford-Shah loss functional in a deep learning framework
* An extensive evaluation of the proposed method on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating its superior performance compared to traditional methods

Overall, this paper presents a novel approach to image segmentation using the Mumford-Shah loss functional, which can be useful for applications where accurate and interpretable segmentation results are crucial, such as medical imaging and object detection.

title: I don't know why this people accept it
text:
I'm just so frustrated with the way people blindly accept things without questioning them. It's like they're just sheep following the herd, without any critical thinking or independent thought.

I mean, take the latest trend in fashion, for example. Everyone's walking around in these ridiculous, overpriced shoes that are completely impractical and uncomfortable. But instead of asking themselves if they really need to spend their hard-earned money on something that's only going to cause them discomfort, they just go along with it because "everyone else is doing it."

And don't even get me started on social media. People are so obsessed with getting likes and followers that they'll post anything and everything, no matter how mundane or narcissistic. They'll even go so far as to buy followers and likes, just to boost their numbers. It's like they're living in some kind of virtual reality where their online persona is more important than their real-life relationships and experiences.

But what really gets me is when people accept things that are clearly harmful or unethical. Like, why do people still support companies that use sweatshop labor or test their products on animals? Don't they realize that their purchasing decisions have real-world consequences?

I guess what I'm trying to say is that I don't understand why people are so willing to accept things without questioning them. Can't they see that there's often more to the story than what's on the surface? And shouldn't they be curious about what's really going on?

I know I can't change the world on my own, but I wish more people would start questioning the status quo and demanding better. We deserve better than to be mindless drones following the crowd.

title: Paul Tillich
text:
Karl Tillich (1886-1965) was a German-American philosophical writer and Christian existentialist writer. He is generally recognized as one of the most important Christian philosophers of the 20th century.

Early Life and Teaching
Tillich was born on May 20, 1886, in Starzeddel, Prussia (now part of Germany). His grandfather was a Protestant minister, and Tillich grew up with a strong political background. He studied philosophy and philosophy at various schools in Austria before gaining his doctorate in theology from the University of Berlin in 1911. He then was a professor in theology at the University of Heidelberg.

Theological Education
In 1914, Tillich started studying at the University of Berlin, where he was friends with the modernist poet Martin Heidegger. During this period, he created his concept of "the ontological coup," which argued that revelation happens when the boundary between being and non-being is transcended. He subsequently came to reject modern religious concepts such as original sin and docetism.

After serving in World War I, Tillich was a teacher of philosophy at the Vienna Institute of Technology, where he taught until 1925. It was during this time that he wrote his last significant work, "Die Cristliche Glaube" ("The Catholic Religion"), which stressed the importance of religion as an act of courage rather than intellectual assent.

In 1927, Tillich left Austria for the United States after the Communist Party returned to power, where he joined the staff of Union Theological College. He was there until 1955, when he transferred to Yale Theological School. At Union, he befriended the Jewish historian Otto Niebuhr, with whom he could participate in a lengthy discussion over how religions should relate to modern society and culture. While Niebuhr supported political equality and activism, Tillich maintained that ultimate concern should be focused only on God.
